title.zh: 卷一百八十二 志第一百三十五 食貨下四
title.raw: 卷一百八十二 志第一百三十五 食貨下四 Volume 182 Treatises 135: Finance and Economics 2d

sentences.zh: 食貨下四○鹽中

translations.literal: Finance and Economics 4 ○ Salt (middle section)
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part Four — Salt Policy (continued)

sentences.zh: 元豐七年，知滄州趙瞻請自大名府、澶、恩、信安、雄、霸、瀛、莫、冀等州盡榷賣以增其利，才半歲，獲息錢十有六萬七千緡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanfeng, Zhao Zhan, who was prefect of Cangzhou, requested that from Daming Prefecture and the prefectures of Chan, En, Xin'an, Xiong, Ba, Ying, Mo, and Ji monopoly sale be fully applied to increase profit; in only half a year, interest money of 167,000 strings was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Yuanfeng reign (1084), Zhao Zhan, prefect of Cangzhou, asked that Daming Prefecture and the prefectures of Chan, En, Xin'an, Xiong, Ba, Ying, Mo, and Ji adopt full government monopoly on salt sales to boost revenue. Within half a year the measure yielded 167,000 strings in interest.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，監察御史王岩叟言：「河北二年以來新行鹽法，所在價增一倍，既奪商賈之利，又增居民之價以為息，聞貧家至以鹽比藥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne, Supervising Censor Wang Yansou said: "For two years in Hebei the new salt law has been in force; everywhere the price has doubled. It has taken profit from merchants while raising the price for residents to generate revenue; I hear that poor households compare salt to medicine.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhezong came to the throne, Supervising Censor Wang Yansou memorialized: "For two years Hebei has operated under the new salt law. Prices have doubled everywhere — merchants have been stripped of their margin while commoners pay more so the state can collect interest. I have heard that the poor now treat salt like medicine.

sentences.zh: 伏惟河朔天下根本，祖宗推此為惠，願陛下不以損民為利，而以益民為利，復鹽法如故，以為河北數百萬生靈無窮之賜。」

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the Hebei region is the foundation of the realm; our ancestors extended this as a benefit. I pray Your Majesty will not take harming the people as profit but take benefiting the people as profit, restore the salt law as before, and regard this as an inexhaustible gift to the millions of living beings in Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: The Hebei heartland is the foundation of the empire; our forebears extended this region special favor in salt policy. I beg Your Majesty to seek profit in benefiting the people, not in burdening them — restore the former salt law as an enduring gift to Hebei's millions."

sentences.zh: 會河北轉運使範子奇奏，鹽稅欲收以十分，遣範鍔商度。

translations.literal: At the same time Hebei Transport Commissioner Fan Ziqi memorialized that salt tax revenue was to be collected at ten-tenths, and Fan E was dispatched to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Hebei transport commissioner Fan Ziqi reported that salt tax collection was to be raised to the full rate, and Fan E was sent to study the change.

sentences.zh: 岩叟復言：「臣在河北，亦知商賈有自請於官，乞罷榷買，願輸倍稅。

translations.literal: Yansou again said: "When I was in Hebei, I also knew that merchants had themselves petitioned the authorities, asking to abolish monopoly purchase and willing to pay double tax.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou added: "During my service in Hebei I learned that merchants themselves had petitioned the government to end monopoly purchase, offering to pay double the tax instead.

sentences.zh: 主計者但知於商賈倍得稅緡以為利，不知商賈將於民間復增賣價以為害也。

translations.literal: Those in charge of accounts only knew that doubling tax strings from merchants was profit; they did not know that merchants would again raise selling prices among the people as harm.
translations.idiomatic: The fiscal officers saw only the doubled tax receipts from merchants as gain; they did not see that merchants would pass the cost on to the populace by raising retail prices — that was the real harm.

sentences.zh: 慶曆六年，既不行三司榷買之法，又不從轉運司增稅之請，仁宗直謂朕慮河北軍民驟食貴鹽，可令依舊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingli, the Three Departments' monopoly-purchase method was not implemented, nor was the transport commission's request to increase tax followed; Emperor Renzong directly said, "I fear that Hebei soldiers and civilians would suddenly eat expensive salt; let it follow the old way."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qingli (1046) the court rejected both the Three Departments' monopoly-purchase scheme and the transport commission's bid to raise taxes. Emperor Renzong said plainly, "I fear Hebei's soldiers and civilians would suddenly face dear salt — let the old arrangements stand."

sentences.zh: 是時計歲增幾六十萬緡，仁宗豈不知為公家之利？

translations.literal: At that time the annual increase was calculated at nearly 600,000 strings; did Emperor Renzong not know this was profit for the state?
translations.idiomatic: The proposed change would have added nearly 600,000 strings a year to the treasury. Did Renzong not understand that was revenue for the state?

sentences.zh: 意謂藏之官不若藏之民。

translations.literal: His meaning was that storing wealth in the government was not as good as storing it among the people.
translations.idiomatic: His view was that wealth held by the people was better than wealth held by the government.

sentences.zh: 今陛下即位之始，宜法仁宗之意，不宜以小利失人心也。」

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of Your Majesty's accession, you should follow Emperor Renzong's intent and should not, for small profit, lose the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Your Majesty's reign you should follow Renzong's example and not sacrifice popular goodwill for petty gain."

sentences.zh: 明年，遂罷河北榷法，仍舊通商。

translations.literal: The next year, the Hebei monopoly law was abolished and free trade in salt was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Hebei salt monopoly was abolished and free commerce in salt was restored.

sentences.zh: 六年，提舉河北鹽稅司請令商賈販鹽，於場務輸稅，以及等戶保任，給小引，量道里為限，即非官監鎮店，聽以使煮之，鹽稅舊額五分者，增為七分。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Hebei Salt Tax Office requested that merchants be allowed to sell salt, pay tax at market offices, and with households of equal rank as guarantors be given small permits limited by distance in li; outside officially supervised market towns they were permitted to have it boiled; where the old salt tax quota was five-tenths, it was raised to seven-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1091) the office charged with Hebei salt taxes proposed letting merchants retail salt, pay tax at market offices, and obtain small transport permits backed by guarantors of equal household rank, with distance limits; outside government-supervised market towns they could arrange boiling. The salt tax rate, formerly five-tenths, was raised to seven-tenths.

sentences.zh: 則鹽稅蓋已行焉。

translations.literal: Thus the salt tax was already in effect.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the salt tax system was already operating.

sentences.zh: 其在兩浙曰杭州場，歲煮七萬七千餘石，明州昌國東、西兩監二十萬一千餘石，秀州場二十萬八千餘石，溫州天富南北監、密鸚永嘉二場，七萬四千餘石，台州黃岩監一萬五千餘石，以給本州及越、處、衢、婺州。

translations.literal: In the Two Zhe regions there was the Hangzhou field, boiling more than 77,000 piculs per year; the eastern and western supervisors of Changguo in Ming Prefecture more than 201,000 piculs; the Xiuzhou field more than 208,000 piculs; the northern and southern Tianfu supervisors and the Miying and Yongjia fields of Wenzhou more than 74,000 piculs; the Huangyan supervisor of Taizhou more than 15,000 piculs — to supply the home prefecture and Yue, Chu, Qu, and Wu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the Two Zhes, the Hangzhou salt works produced over 77,000 piculs yearly; Ming's eastern and western Changguo supervisors over 201,000; Xiuzhou over 208,000; Wenzhou's northern and southern Tianfu supervisors plus the Miying and Yongjia fields over 74,000; and Taizhou's Huangyan supervisor over 15,000 — supplying their home prefectures plus Yue, Chu, Qu, and Wu.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，杭、秀、溫、台、明各監一，溫州又領場三，而一路歲課視舊減六萬八千石，以給本路及江東之歙州。

translations.literal: During the Tiansheng era, Hang, Xiu, Wen, Tai, and Ming each had one supervisor; Wenzhou also oversaw three fields, while the circuit's annual quota was reduced by 68,000 piculs compared with the old amount, to supply the home circuit and She Prefecture in Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Renzong's Tiansheng reign each of Hang, Xiu, Wen, Tai, and Ming had one supervisor; Wenzhou also administered three fields. The circuit's annual salt quota fell by 68,000 piculs from earlier levels, with output allocated to the circuit itself and She Prefecture in Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 慶曆初，製置司言：比年河流淺涸，漕運艱阻，靡費益甚，請量增江、淮、兩浙、荊湖六路糶鹽錢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingli, the Fiscal Planning Office said: In recent years rivers have been shallow and dry, grain transport difficult, and waste increasingly severe; it requested a measured increase in the price of sold salt money in the six circuits of Jiang, Huai, Two Zhe, and Jing-Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qingli era the fiscal planning office reported that rivers had run shallow, making grain transport costly and wasteful, and asked to raise somewhat the price of government salt sold in the Jiang, Huai, Two Zhe, and Jing-Hu circuits.

sentences.zh: 下三司議，三司奏荊湖已嘗增錢，餘四路三十八州軍，請斤增二錢或四錢。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Three Departments for deliberation; the Three Departments memorialized that Jing-Hu had already had its price raised, and for the remaining four circuits' thirty-eight prefectures and armies requested an increase of two or four cash per jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments were consulted. They replied that Jing-Hu had already seen a price hike and proposed raising the price by two or four cash per jin in the other four circuits' thirty-eight prefectures and military commands.

sentences.zh: 詔俟河流通運復故。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that this await restoration of river transport to the former condition.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the increase deferred until river transport returned to normal.

sentences.zh: 既而江州置轉般倉，益置漕船及傭客舟以運，製置司因請六路五十一州軍斤增五錢。

translations.literal: Subsequently a transfer warehouse was established at Jiang Prefecture, and more transport ships and hired merchant vessels were added for carriage; the Fiscal Planning Office therefore requested a five-cash increase per jin in fifty-one prefectures and armies of the six circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Later a transfer depot was set up at Jiangzhou, with more transport vessels and hired merchant boats added; the planning office then asked for a five-cash-per-jin increase across fifty-one prefectures and commands in the six circuits.

sentences.zh: 民苦官鹽估高，無以為食，諸路皆言其不便。

translations.literal: The people suffered because official salt was priced high and they had nothing to eat with it; every circuit said it was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The people struggled under high official salt prices and could scarcely afford salt for their meals; every circuit reported hardship.

sentences.zh: 久之，韓絳安撫江南還，亦極言之。

translations.literal: After a long time, Han Jiang, returning from pacifying Jiangnan, also spoke of it with utmost force.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Han Jiang, back from his Jiangnan pacification assignment, spoke out strongly on the same point.

sentences.zh: 其後兩浙轉運使沈立、李肅之奏：「本路鹽課緡錢歲七十九萬，嘉祐三年，才及五十三萬；

translations.literal: Later the Two Zhe transport commissioners Shen Li and Li Suzhi memorialized: "This circuit's salt revenue in strings was 790,000 per year; in the third year of Jiayou it reached only 530,000;
translations.idiomatic: Later the Two Zhe transport commissioners Shen Li and Li Suzhi reported: "Annual salt revenue for this circuit had been 790,000 strings; in the third year of Jiayou (1058) it fell to only 530,000;

sentences.zh: 而一歲之內，私販坐罪者三千九十九人；

translations.literal: yet within one year those convicted of illegal private sale numbered 3,099 persons;
translations.idiomatic: yet in a single year 3,099 people were convicted of illegal private salt trade;

sentences.zh: 弊在於官鹽估高，故私販不止，而官課益虧。

translations.literal: the harm lay in official salt being priced high, so private sale did not cease, while official revenue grew ever more deficient.
translations.idiomatic: the trouble is that official salt is overpriced, private trade never stops, and government revenue keeps falling.

sentences.zh: 請裁官估，罷鹽綱，令鋪戶衙前自趨山場取鹽，如此則鹽善而估平，人不肯冒禁私售，官課必溢。」

translations.literal: They requested cutting official valuation, abolishing salt transport convoys, and letting shop households and yamen runners go themselves to mountain fields to fetch salt; thus salt would be good and valuation level, people would not dare to violate the ban and sell privately, and official revenue would surely overflow."
translations.idiomatic: They asked to lower official prices, abolish the salt transport convoys, and let shopkeepers and yamen runners fetch salt directly from the production sites — then salt quality would improve, prices would stabilize, people would not risk illegal sales, and government revenue would surely rise."

sentences.zh: 發運司難之。

translations.literal: The Commissary Transport Office objected.
translations.idiomatic: The commissary transport office objected.

sentences.zh: 立、肅之固請試用其法二三年，可見利害，詔可。

translations.literal: Li and Suzhi firmly requested trial use of their method for two or three years so that benefit and harm could be seen; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li and Li Suzhi pressed to trial the plan for two or three years to judge results; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 立嘗論東鹽利害，條亭戶、倉場、漕運之弊，謂：「愛恤亭戶使不至困窮，休息漕卒使有以為生，防製倉場使不為掊克率斂，絕私販，減官估，果能行此五者，歲可增緡錢一二百萬。」

translations.literal: Li once discussed the benefit and harm of eastern salt, listing the abuses of saltern households, warehouses, and grain transport, saying: "If one cherishes saltern households so they do not reach destitution, gives rest to transport laborers so they have means to live, guards warehouses so they do not extort and levy, cuts off private sale, and reduces official valuation — if these five can truly be carried out, annually one or two million strings can be added."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li had analyzed eastern salt policy, detailing abuses against saltern households, depot officials, and transport workers. He argued: "Care for saltern households so they are not ruined; ease transport laborers so they can earn a living; stop depot extortion; end illegal trade; cut official prices — if all five are enforced, annual revenue could rise by one or two million strings."

sentences.zh: 集《鹽策》二十卷以進，其言亭戶困乏尤甚。

translations.literal: He compiled twenty juan of Salt Policies and presented them; his words on the extreme destitution of saltern households were especially forceful.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a twenty-juan compilation, Salt Policies, stressing above all the dire poverty of saltern households.

sentences.zh: 然自皇祐以來，屢下詔書輒及之，命給亭戶官本，皆以實錢；

translations.literal: Yet from Huangyou onward, edicts repeatedly addressed this, ordering that official capital be given to saltern households, all in real cash;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Huangyou era (1049–1053) repeated edicts had ordered official advance payments to saltern households in hard cash;

sentences.zh: 其售額外鹽者，給粟帛必糧；

translations.literal: for those selling salt beyond quota, grain and cloth given must be grain;
translations.idiomatic: for salt sold above quota, payment in grain and cloth had to be actual grain;

sentences.zh: 亭戶逋歲課久不能輸者，悉蠲之。

translations.literal: saltern households long unable to deliver overdue annual quotas were all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: and long-overdue annual quotas that saltern households could not pay were wholly forgiven.

sentences.zh: 所以存恤之意甚厚，而有司罕有承順焉。

translations.literal: Thus the intent to preserve and comfort was very generous, yet the responsible offices rarely complied.
translations.idiomatic: The court's intent to protect them was generous, but local officials rarely complied.

sentences.zh: 熙寧以來，杭、秀、溫、台、明五州共領監六、場十有四，然鹽價苦高，私販者眾，轉為盜賊，課額大失。

translations.literal: Since Xining, the five prefectures Hang, Xiu, Wen, Tai, and Ming jointly oversaw six supervisors and fourteen fields, yet salt prices were painfully high, private sellers numerous, many turning into bandits, and revenue quotas greatly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xining reforms (1068 onward), Hang, Xiu, Wen, Tai, and Ming together ran six supervisors and fourteen fields, but salt prices stayed painfully high, illegal trade flourished, many smugglers turned to banditry, and revenue quotas collapsed.

sentences.zh: 二年，有萬奇者獻言欲撲兩浙鹽而與民，乃遣奇從發運使薛向詢度利害。

translations.literal: In the second year, a Wan Qi presented a proposal to abolish Two Zhe salt monopoly and give it to the people; Qi was then sent with Commissary Transport Commissioner Xue Xiang to inquire into benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1069) a man named Wan Qi proposed abolishing the Two Zhes salt monopoly and returning trade to the people; Wan Qi was sent with commissary transport commissioner Xue Xiang to study the idea.

sentences.zh: 神宗以問王安石，對曰：「趙抃言衢州撲鹽，所收課敵兩浙路，抃但見衢、湖可撲，不知衢鹽侵饒、信，湖鹽侵廣德、升州，故課可增，如蘇、常則難比衢、湖。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong asked Wang Anshi, who replied: "Zhao Bian said that abolishing salt monopoly in Quzhou would yield revenue rivaling the whole Two Zhe circuit; Bian only saw that Qu and Hu could be abolished, not knowing that Qu salt encroached on Rao and Xin, and Hu salt on Guangde and Sheng Prefecture — hence revenue could increase; for Su and Chang it would be hard to compare with Qu and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong asked Wang Anshi, who replied: "Zhao Bian claimed that ending the monopoly in Quzhou alone could match all Two Zhe revenue. Bian saw only Qu and Hu as candidates; he did not see that Qu salt competes with Rao and Xin, and Hu salt with Guangde and Sheng — so revenue might rise there, but Su and Chang cannot be compared to Qu and Hu.

sentences.zh: 今宜製置煎鹽亭戶及差鹽地人戶督捕私販，般運以時，嚴察拌和，則鹽法自舉，毋事改製。」

translations.literal: Now one should arrange saltern households who boil salt and assign salt-region households to supervise capture of private sellers, transport on schedule, and strictly inspect mixing — then the salt law will raise itself; there is no need to change the system."
translations.idiomatic: The right course is to organize boiling households, assign local residents to hunt smugglers, keep transport on schedule, and strictly police adulteration — then the salt law will work without systemic overhaul."

sentences.zh: 五年，以盧秉權發遣兩浙提點刑獄，仍專提舉鹽事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Lu Bing was appointed with authority as dispatched Two Zhe Judicial Intendant, while still exclusively charged with salt affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1072) Lu Bing was dispatched as acting Two Zhe judicial intendant with sole charge of salt administration.

sentences.zh: 秉前與著作佐郎曾默行淮南、兩浙，詢究利害。

translations.literal: Bing had earlier traveled Huainan and the Two Zhes with Assistant Academician Zeng Mo, investigating benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Bing had earlier toured Huainan and the Two Zhes with assistant academician Zeng Mo to study the system's strengths and flaws.

sentences.zh: 異時灶戶煮鹽，與官為市，鹽場不時償其直，灶戶益困。

translations.literal: In former times saltern households boiled salt and traded with the government; salt fields did not pay their price on time, and saltern households grew ever more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Previously saltern households boiled salt and sold to the state, but depots often delayed payment, deepening their hardship.

sentences.zh: 秉先請儲發運司錢及雜錢百萬緡以待償，而諸場皆定分數：錢塘縣楊村場上接睦、歙等州，與越州錢清場等，水勢稍淺，以六分為額；

translations.literal: Bing first requested storing one million strings from commissary transport funds and miscellaneous funds to await payment, while every field was assigned a quota share: Yangcun field in Qiantang County, bordering Mu and She prefectures, with Yue Prefecture's Qianqing field and others where water was somewhat shallow, took six-tenths as quota;
translations.idiomatic: Bing first asked to set aside one million strings from transport and miscellaneous funds for prompt payment, and fixed quota shares for each field: Yangcun in Qiantang, bordering Mu and She, with Yue's Qianqing and similar shallow-water sites, at six-tenths;

sentences.zh: 楊村下接仁和之湯村為七分；

translations.literal: below Yangcun, bordering Renhe's Tangcun, was seven-tenths;
translations.idiomatic: Yangcun's downstream link to Renhe's Tangcun at seven-tenths;

sentences.zh: 鹽官場為八分；

translations.literal: the Yanguan field was eight-tenths;
translations.idiomatic: the Yanguan field at eight-tenths;

sentences.zh: 並海而東為越州餘姚縣石堰場、明州慈溪縣鳴鶴場皆九分；

translations.literal: along the coast eastward, Yuyao County's Shiyan field in Yue Prefecture and Cixi's Minghe field in Ming Prefecture were both nine-tenths;
translations.idiomatic: east along the coast, Yue's Yuyao Shiyan and Ming's Cixi Minghe at nine-tenths each;

sentences.zh: 至岱山、昌國，又東南為溫州雙穗、南天富、北天富場為十分；

translations.literal: reaching Daishan and Changguo, and further southeast the Shuanghui, southern Tianfu, and northern Tianfu fields of Wenzhou were ten-tenths;
translations.idiomatic: at Daishan and Changguo, and southeast to Wenzhou's Shuanghui, southern Tianfu, and northern Tianfu at the full ten-tenths;

sentences.zh: 蓋其分數約得鹽多寡而為之節。

translations.literal: generally the shares were calibrated to the relative amount of salt obtained.
translations.idiomatic: the shares were scaled roughly to each site's salt yield.

sentences.zh: 自岱山以及二天富煉以海水，所得為最多。

translations.literal: From Daishan through the two Tianfu sites, boiling with seawater yielded the most.
translations.idiomatic: From Daishan through the two Tianfu fields, seawater boiling yielded the most salt.

sentences.zh: 由鳴鶴西南及湯村則刮堿淋鹵，十得六七。

translations.literal: From Minghe southwest to Tangcun they scraped alkali and leached brine, obtaining six or seven from ten.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest from Minghe through Tangcun they scraped alkali and leached brine, recovering six or seven parts in ten.

sentences.zh: 鹽官、湯村用鐵盤，故鹽色青白；

translations.literal: Yanguan and Tangcun used iron pans, so the salt was bluish-white;
translations.idiomatic: Yanguan and Tangcun used iron pans, producing bluish-white salt;

sentences.zh: 楊村及錢清場織竹為盤，塗以石灰，故色少黃；

translations.literal: Yangcun and the Qianqing field wove bamboo into pans and coated them with lime, so the color was somewhat yellow;
translations.idiomatic: Yangcun and Qianqing wove bamboo pans coated with lime, giving a slightly yellow cast;

sentences.zh: 石堰以東近海水咸，故雖用竹盤，而鹽色尤白。

translations.literal: east of Shiyan, near the sea where water was salty, even though bamboo pans were used, the salt color was especially white.
translations.idiomatic: east of Shiyan, where seawater is especially briny, even bamboo-pan salt came out exceptionally white.

sentences.zh: 秉因定伏火盤數以絕私煮，自三灶至十灶為一甲，而煮鹽地什伍其民，以相幾察；

translations.literal: Bing therefore fixed the number of dormant-fire pans to cut off private boiling; from three to ten stoves formed one company, and in salt-boiling areas the people were grouped in fives and tens for mutual surveillance;
translations.idiomatic: Bing fixed the number of licensed boiling pans to stop illegal production, grouped three to ten stoves into one unit, and organized saltern populations in mutual surveillance groups;

sentences.zh: 及募酒坊戶願占課額，取鹽於官賣之，月以錢輸官，毋得越所酤地；

translations.literal: and recruited wine-shop households willing to assume revenue quotas, taking salt from the government to sell it, paying money monthly to the government, not permitted to cross their licensed selling area;
translations.idiomatic: and recruited wine-shop operators to assume sales quotas, buy salt from the state, pay monthly, and stay within licensed territories;

sentences.zh: 而又嚴捕盜販者，罪不至配，雖杖者皆同妻子遷五百里。

translations.literal: while strictly capturing smugglers; even when punishment did not reach exile, those merely flogged were all relocated with wives and children five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He also cracked down on smugglers: even when punishment fell short of exile, those merely flogged were relocated with their families five hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 仍益開封府界、京東兵各五百人防捕。

translations.literal: Still more, five hundred troops each from the Kaifeng circuit and Jingdong were added for capture and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred additional troops each from the Kaifeng metropolitan zone and Jingdong were assigned to enforcement.

sentences.zh: 時惟杭、越、湖三州格新法不行，發運司劾奏虧課，皆獄治。

translations.literal: At the time only Hang, Yue, and Hu prefectures resisted implementing the new law; the transport office impeached them for revenue shortfalls, and all were prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hang, Yue, and Hu still resisted the new law; the transport office impeached them for revenue shortfalls and all were prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 王安石為神宗言捕鹽法急，可以止刑。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi told Shenzong that urgent enforcement of the salt-capture law could stop punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi told Shenzong that strict salt enforcement would eventually reduce criminal penalties.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃詔兩浙提舉鹽事司，諸州虧課者未得遽劾，以增虧及違法輕重分三等以聞。

translations.literal: After a long time, an edict ordered the Two Zhe Salt Affairs Office that prefectures with revenue shortfalls might not be immediately impeached; according to increase or shortfall and severity of violation, three grades were to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually the court ordered the Two Zhe salt office not to impeach prefectures immediately for revenue shortfalls, but to report three grades by severity of loss and violation.

sentences.zh: 七年，以盧秉鹽課雖增，刑獄實繁，慮無辜即罪者眾，徙其職淮南，以江東漕臣張靚代之，且休量其事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, because Lu Bing's salt revenue had increased but criminal cases were truly numerous, fearing many innocents were convicted, his post was moved to Huainan; Jiangdong transport official Zhang Jing replaced him, and the matter was paused for reassessment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1074), though Lu Bing had raised salt revenue, criminal cases had multiplied and many feared wrongful conviction; he was transferred to Huainan, replaced by Jiangdong transport official Zhang Jing, and the program was paused for review.

sentences.zh: 靚言秉在事，越州監催鹽償至有母殺子者，詔劾其罪，然竟免，仍以增課擢太常博士，升一資。

translations.literal: Jing said that while Bing was in office, Yue Prefecture supervisors pressing salt payment had cases even of mothers killing sons; an edict investigated his crime, yet in the end he was excused and still promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices for increasing revenue, advancing one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing reported that under Bing's tenure Yue supervisors pressing salt payments drove cases as extreme as mothers killing sons. An investigation was ordered, yet Bing was excused and promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices for raising revenue, advancing one grade.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，三司言兩浙漕司寬弛，鹽息大虧，命著作佐郎翁仲通更議措置。

translations.literal: After more than a year, the Three Departments said the Two Zhe transport office was lax, salt interest greatly deficient, and ordered Assistant Academician Weng Zhongtong to deliberate anew on arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Three Departments reported that Two Zhe transport officials had grown lax and salt profits had collapsed; assistant academician Weng Zhongtong was ordered to redesign the system.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，言者論秉推行浙西鹽法，務誅利以增課，所配流者至一萬二千餘人，秉坐降職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, critics said Bing in enforcing western Zhe salt law pursued profit by punishment to increase revenue; those exiled reached more than 12,000 persons, and Bing was demoted for it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era (1086) critics charged that Bing's western Zhe salt policy pursued revenue through harsh punishment, exiling more than 12,000 people; Bing was demoted.

sentences.zh: 兩浙鹽亭戶計丁輸鹽，逋負滋廣，二年，詔蠲之。

translations.literal: Two Zhe saltern households delivered salt by registered males; arrears grew ever wider; in the second year, an edict remitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Two Zhe saltern households owed salt by household head count; arrears kept mounting until the second year (1087), when an edict forgave them.

sentences.zh: 後更積負無以償，元符初，察訪使以狀聞，有司乃以朝旨不行，右正言鄒浩嘗極疏其害。

translations.literal: Later arrears again accumulated with no means to pay; at the beginning of Yuanfu, investigation commissioners reported the situation; the responsible offices said court orders were not carried out; Right Remonstrator Zou Hao once memorialized at length on the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Arrears piled up again beyond repayment; early in the Yuanfu era (1098) investigators reported that court orders were ignored; Right Remonstrator Zou Hao had memorialized at length on the harm.

sentences.zh: 明州鳴鶴場鹽課弗登，撥隸越州。

translations.literal: The Ming Prefecture Minghe field failed to meet salt revenue; it was reassigned to Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Prefecture's Minghe salt field failed to meet its quota and was reassigned to Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，樓異為明州，請仍舊，且於接近台州給舊鹽五七萬囊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, Lou Yi was prefect of Ming and requested restoration of the former arrangement, and moreover that from nearby Taizhou 50,000 to 70,000 bags of old salt be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanhe (1119), Lou Yi as Ming prefect asked to restore the former arrangement and receive 50,000 to 70,000 bags of legacy salt from nearby Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「明州鹽場三，昨以施置不善，以鳴鶴一場隸越，客始輻湊。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Ming Prefecture has three salt fields; because arrangements were poorly made yesterday, one Minghe field was subordinated to Yue, and merchants only then gathered in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The court replied: "Ming has three salt fields. Poor planning led us to subordinate Minghe to Yue, and only then did merchants converge.

sentences.zh: 猶有二場積鹽以百萬計，未見功緒，此而不圖，東欲取於越，西欲取於台，改令害法，動搖眾情。」

translations.literal: Yet the other two fields still have accumulated salt on the order of a million, with no sign of results. If this is not planned for, in the east you wish to take from Yue, in the west from Tai — changing orders harms the law and shakes popular sentiment."
translations.idiomatic: The other two fields still hold a million bags in stock with little progress. If we do not address this, Ming will seek supply from Yue in the east and Taizhou in the west — constant rule changes undermine the law and unsettle the trade."

sentences.zh: 令狀析以聞。

translations.literal: He was ordered to submit a detailed memorial reporting up.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to submit a detailed report.

sentences.zh: 其在淮南曰楚州鹽城監，歲煮四十一萬七千餘石，通州豐利監四十八萬九千餘石，泰州海陵監如皋倉小海場六十五萬六千餘石，各給本州及淮南之廬和舒蘄黃州、無為軍，江南之江寧府、宣、洪、袁、吉、筠、江、池、太、平、饒、信、歙、撫州、廣德臨江軍，兩浙之常、潤、湖、睦州，荊湖之江陵府、安、復、潭、鼎、嶽、鄂、衡、永州、漢陽軍。

translations.literal: In Huainan there was Chuzhou's Yancheng supervisor, boiling more than 417,000 piculs yearly; Tongzhou's Fengli supervisor more than 489,000 piculs; Taizhou's Hailing supervisor with Rugao warehouse and Xiaohai field more than 656,000 piculs — each supplying its home prefecture and Huainan's Lu, He, Shu, Qi, and Huang prefectures and Wuwei Army; Jiangnan's Jiangning Prefecture, Xuan, Hong, Yuan, Ji, Jun, Jiang, Chi, Tai, Ping, Rao, Xin, She, and Fu prefectures, Guangde and Linjiang armies; the Two Zhes' Chang, Run, Hu, and Mu prefectures; Jing-Hu's Jiangling Prefecture, An, Fu, Tan, Ding, Yue, E, Heng, Yong Prefecture, and Hanyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Huainan: Chuzhou's Yancheng supervisor produced over 417,000 piculs yearly; Tongzhou's Fengli over 489,000; Taizhou's Hailing with Rugao depot and Xiaohai field over 656,000 — supplying their home prefectures plus Huainan's Lu, He, Shu, Qi, and Huang and Wuwei Army; Jiangnan's Jiangning, Xuan, Hong, Yuan, Ji, Jun, Jiang, Chi, Tai, Ping, Rao, Xin, She, and Fu, Guangde and Linjiang; the Two Zhes' Chang, Run, Hu, and Mu; and Jing-Hu's Jiangling, An, Fu, Tan, Ding, Yue, E, Heng, Yong, and Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 海州板浦、惠澤、洛要三場歲煮四十七萬七千餘石，漣水軍海口場十一萬五千餘石，各給本州軍及京東之徐州，淮南之光、泗、濠、壽州，兩浙之杭、蘇、湖、常、潤州、江陰軍。

translations.literal: Haizhou's Banpu, Huize, and Luoyao three fields boiled more than 477,000 piculs yearly; Lianshui Army's Haikou field more than 115,000 piculs — each supplying its home prefecture or army and Jingdong's Xuzhou, Huainan's Guang, Si, Hao, and Shou prefectures, and the Two Zhes' Hang, Su, Hu, Chang, Run prefectures and Jiangyin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Haizhou's Banpu, Huize, and Luoyao fields boiled over 477,000 piculs yearly; Lianshui Army's Haikou over 115,000 — supplying their home commands plus Jingdong's Xuzhou, Huainan's Guang, Si, Hao, and Shou, and the Two Zhes' Hang, Su, Hu, Chang, Run, and Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，通、楚州場各七，泰州場八，海州場二，漣水軍場一，歲煮視舊減六十九萬七千五百四十餘石，以給本路及江南東西、荊湖南北四路，舊並給兩浙路，天聖七年始罷。

translations.literal: During Tiansheng, Tong and Chu prefectures each had seven fields, Taizhou eight fields, Haizhou two fields, Lianshui Army one field; annual boiling was reduced by 697,540 piculs compared with the old amount, to supply the home circuit and the four circuits of Jiangnan East and West and Jing-Hu South and North; formerly it also supplied the Two Zhe circuit, which ceased in the seventh year of Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiansheng, Tong and Chu had seven fields each, Taizhou eight, Haizhou two, Lianshui one; annual output fell by 697,540 piculs from earlier levels to supply the home circuit and Jiangnan east and west and Jing-Hu south and north. Formerly Two Zhe was also supplied until the seventh year of Tiansheng (1029).

sentences.zh: 凡鹽之入，置倉以受之，通、楚州各一，泰州三，以受三州鹽。

translations.literal: Whenever salt entered, warehouses were set up to receive it: Tong and Chu prefectures each one, Taizhou three, to receive salt from the three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Incoming salt was received at warehouses: one each at Tong and Chu, three at Taizhou for the three prefectures' output.

sentences.zh: 又置轉般倉二，一於真州，以受通、泰、楚五倉鹽；

translations.literal: Two transfer warehouses were also set up, one at Zhen Prefecture to receive salt from the five warehouses of Tong, Tai, and Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Two transfer depots were added: one at Zhenzhou receiving salt from Tong, Tai, and Chu's five warehouses;

sentences.zh: 一於漣水軍，以受海州漣水鹽。

translations.literal: one at Lianshui Army to receive salt from Haizhou and Lianshui.
translations.idiomatic: one at Lianshui Army for Haizhou and Lianshui salt.

sentences.zh: 江南、荊湖歲漕米至淮南，受鹽以歸。

translations.literal: Jiangnan and Jing-Hu annually transported grain to Huainan and received salt in return.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Jiangnan and Jing-Hu sent tribute grain to Huainan and took salt back in exchange.

sentences.zh: 東南鹽利，視天下為最厚。

translations.literal: Southeastern salt profit was regarded as the richest in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Southeastern salt profits were the richest in the empire.

sentences.zh: 鹽之入官，淮南、福建、兩浙之溫、台、明斤為錢四，杭、秀為錢六，廣南為錢五。

translations.literal: For salt entering government hands, Huainan, Fujian, and Wen, Tai, and Ming of the Two Zhes were four cash per jin; Hang and Xiu six cash; Guangnan five cash.
translations.idiomatic: Salt paid to the state was priced at four cash per jin in Huainan, Fujian, and Wen, Tai, and Ming in the Two Zhes; six in Hang and Xiu; five in Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 其出，視去鹽道里遠近而上下其估，利有至十倍者。

translations.literal: On distribution, valuation was raised or lowered according to distance from the salt route in li; profit sometimes reached tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: Retail prices varied with distance from the source, and markups could reach tenfold.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，參知政事王隨建言：「淮南鹽初甚善。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao, Vice Grand Councilor Wang Sui memorialized: "Huainan salt was at first very good.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao (1033), Vice Grand Councilor Wang Sui proposed: "Huainan salt was once excellent.

sentences.zh: 自通、泰、楚運至真州，自真州運至江、浙、荊湖，綱吏舟卒，侵盜販煮，從而雜以沙土。

translations.literal: From Tong, Tai, and Chu it was transported to Zhen Prefecture, and from Zhen to Jiang, Zhe, and Jing-Hu; convoy clerks and boat laborers stole, sold, and boiled illicitly, then mixed in sand and soil.
translations.idiomatic: Transported from Tong, Tai, and Chu to Zhenzhou, then onward to Jiang, Zhe, and Jing-Hu, convoy clerks and boatmen stole, resold, and illicitly boiled salt, adulterating it with sand and dirt.

sentences.zh: 涉道愈遠，雜惡殆不可食，吏卒坐鞭笞，徒配相繼而莫能止。

translations.literal: The farther the route, the more adulterated and foul it became, nearly inedible; clerks and laborers were flogged and exiled in succession yet it could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The farther it traveled, the fouler it grew, nearly inedible — officials flogged and exiled men in succession yet could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 比歲運河淺涸，漕挽不行，遠州村民，頓乏鹽食；

translations.literal: In recent years the transport canals were shallow and dry, grain towing could not proceed, and villagers in distant prefectures suddenly lacked salt to eat;
translations.idiomatic: In recent years canals ran shallow, grain transport stalled, and distant villages suddenly lacked salt;

sentences.zh: 而淮南所積一千五百萬石，至無屋以貯，則露積苫覆，歲以損耗。

translations.literal: yet Huainan had accumulated fifteen million piculs, until there were no buildings to store it, and it was piled in the open and covered with mats, losing value yearly to waste.
translations.idiomatic: while Huainan sat on fifteen million piculs with no warehouse space, salt piled in the open under mats and wasted away each year.

sentences.zh: 又亭戶輸鹽，應得本錢或無以給，故亭戶貧困，往往起為盜賊，其害如此。

translations.literal: Moreover saltern households delivered salt but sometimes received no capital payment due them, so saltern households were impoverished and often rose as bandits — the harm was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Saltern households delivered salt but often went unpaid, grew destitute, and frequently turned to banditry — such was the damage.

sentences.zh: 願權聽通商三五年，使商人入錢京師，又置折博務於揚州，使輸錢及粟帛，計直予鹽。

translations.literal: I wish temporarily to permit free trade for three to five years, let merchants pay money into the capital, and also set up an exchange office at Yangzhou so they pay money and grain or cloth, calculating value and granting salt.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to permit free salt trade for three to five years, let merchants pay cash in the capital, and establish an exchange office at Yangzhou where they pay cash, grain, or cloth and receive salt at calculated value.

sentences.zh: 鹽一石約售錢二千，則一千五百萬石可得緡錢三千萬以資國用，一利也；

translations.literal: If one picul of salt sold for about 2,000 cash, then fifteen million piculs could yield thirty million strings for state use — the first benefit;
translations.idiomatic: At roughly 2,000 cash per picul, fifteen million piculs would yield thirty million strings for state use — a first benefit;

sentences.zh: 江、湖遠近皆食白鹽，二利也；

translations.literal: near and far on the rivers and lakes all would eat white salt — the second benefit;
translations.idiomatic: near and far along the rivers and lakes all would get good white salt — a second benefit;

sentences.zh: 歲罷漕運糜費，風水覆溺，舟人不陷刑辟，三利也；

translations.literal: yearly abolition of transport waste, wind and water capsizing, boatmen not falling under criminal punishment — the third benefit;
translations.idiomatic: ending annual transport waste, shipwrecks, and criminal punishment for boatmen — a third benefit;

sentences.zh: 昔時漕鹽舟可移以漕米，四利也；

translations.literal: formerly salt transport vessels could be shifted to transport grain — the fourth benefit;
translations.idiomatic: former salt transport vessels could carry grain instead — a fourth benefit;

sentences.zh: 商人入錢，可取以償亭戶，五利也。」

translations.literal: merchant payments could be taken to compensate saltern households — the fifth benefit."
translations.idiomatic: merchant payments could reimburse saltern households — a fifth benefit."

sentences.zh: 康定元年，詔商人入芻粟陝西並邊，願受東南鹽者加數與之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding, an edict ordered that merchants delivering fodder grain to Shaanxi and the border who wished to receive southeastern salt should be given an increased allotment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangding (1040) merchants delivering fodder to Shaanxi and the border who chose southeastern salt received an extra allotment.

sentences.zh: 會河北穀賤，三司因請內地諸州行三說法，亦以鹽代京師所給緡錢，糴二十萬石止。

translations.literal: As Hebei grain was cheap, the Three Departments therefore requested inland prefectures to implement the three-exchange method, also using salt in place of strings paid from the capital, purchasing only 200,000 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei grain prices fell, the Three Departments asked inland prefectures to adopt the three-exchange method, substituting salt for capital cash payments, limited to 200,000 piculs of grain purchase.

sentences.zh: 慶曆二年，又詔：「入中陝西、河東者持券至京師，償以錢及金帛各半之；

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingli, another edict said: "Those who delivered goods to Shaanxi and Hedong and brought certificates to the capital were repaid half in cash and half in gold and silk;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingli (1042) another edict ruled: "Deliverers to Shaanxi and Hedong who brought certificates to the capital would be paid half in cash and half in gold and silk;

sentences.zh: 不願受金帛者予茶鹽、香藥，惟其所欲。」

translations.literal: those unwilling to receive gold and silk were given tea, salt, and aromatics as they wished."
translations.idiomatic: those who declined gold and silk could take tea, salt, or aromatics as they preferred."

sentences.zh: 而東南鹽利厚，商旅皆願得鹽。

translations.literal: Yet southeastern salt profit was thick, and traveling merchants all wished to receive salt.
translations.idiomatic: Southeastern salt profits were rich, and merchants all preferred salt.

sentences.zh: 八年，河北行四說法，鹽居其一，而並邊芻粟，皆有虛估，騰踴至數倍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Hebei implemented the four-exchange method, salt being one part; borderland fodder grain all had inflated valuations, surging to several times.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1048) Hebei adopted the four-exchange method with salt as one component; borderland fodder valuations were inflated several times over.

sentences.zh: 券至京師，反為蓄賈所抑，鹽百八斤舊售錢十萬，至是六萬，商人以賤估售券取鹽，不復入錢京師，帑藏益乏。

translations.literal: When certificates reached the capital they were instead suppressed by hoarding merchants; 108 jin of salt formerly sold for 100,000 cash, now 60,000; merchants sold certificates at low valuation to take salt and no longer paid money into the capital, and the treasury grew ever more deficient.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital hoarding merchants depressed certificate values; 108 jin of salt that had sold for 100,000 cash now fetched 60,000. Merchants sold certificates cheaply to claim salt and stopped paying cash in the capital, draining the treasury further.

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年，復入錢京師法，視舊錢數稍增予鹽，而並邊入中先得券受鹽者，河東、陝西入芻粟直錢十萬，止給鹽直七萬河北又損為六萬五千，且令入錢十萬於京師，乃聽兼給，謂之對貼，自是入錢京師稍復故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangyou, the method of paying money into the capital was restored; according to the old cash amount salt granted was slightly increased. For those on the border who first received certificates and took salt, for Hedong and Shaanxi delivering fodder worth 100,000 cash only 70,000 in salt value was given; Hebei was further reduced to 65,000; moreover they were ordered to pay 100,000 cash into the capital before combined payment was permitted — called "matching paste"; from this paying money into the capital gradually returned toward the former state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangyou (1050) the capital cash-payment system was restored with slightly more salt per old cash amount. Border deliverers who took salt on certificate first received only 70,000 in salt value for 100,000 in fodder in Hedong and Shaanxi, and 65,000 in Hebei; they also had to deposit 100,000 cash in the capital before receiving the full payment — called "matching paste." Capital cash payments gradually recovered.

sentences.zh: 初，天聖九年，三司請榷貨務入錢售東南鹽，以百八十萬三千緡為額，後增至四百萬緡。

translations.literal: Initially, in the ninth year of Tiansheng, the Three Departments requested that the monopoly goods office accept cash payments to sell southeastern salt, fixing the quota at 1,803,000 strings of cash, later increased to 4,000,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the ninth year of Tiansheng the Three Departments asked the monopoly goods office to take cash for southeastern salt sales, with a quota of 1,803,000 strings that was later raised to 4,000,000.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，諸路漕運不足，榷貨務課益不登，於是即發運司置官專領運鹽公事。

translations.literal: During Jiayou, circuit grain transport was insufficient, and the monopoly goods office revenue increasingly failed to meet its targets; thereupon the Directorate of Consignment Transport established officials to take charge exclusively of salt transport affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiayou era transport from the circuits fell short and monopoly goods office receipts kept missing their targets, so the consignment transport directorate appointed officials solely responsible for moving salt.

sentences.zh: 治平中，京師入緡錢二百二十七萬，而淮南、兩浙、福建、江南、荊湖、廣南六路歲售緡錢，皇祐中二百七十三萬，治平中三百二十九萬。

translations.literal: During Zhiping, the capital received 2,270,000 strings of cash, while Huainan, Liang-Zhe, Fujian, Jiangnan, Jing-Hu, and Guangnan — the six circuits — sold annually: in Huangyou 2,730,000 strings, in Zhiping 3,290,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhiping the capital took in 2,270,000 strings, while annual sales in the six southeastern circuits — Huainan, Liang-Zhe, Fujian, Jiangnan, Jing-Hu, and Guangnan — rose from 2,730,000 strings in Huangyou to 3,290,000 in Zhiping.

sentences.zh: 江、湖運鹽既雜惡，官估復高，故百姓利食私鹽，而並海民以魚鹽為業，用工省而得利厚。

translations.literal: Salt transported from the Jiang and Hu regions was already adulterated and poor in quality, and the official assessment was again high; therefore common people found it profitable to eat private salt, while coastal people took fish-and-salt as their livelihood, with less labor and thick profit.
translations.idiomatic: Official salt shipped through the Jiang and Hu basins was adulterated and overpriced, so people turned to illicit salt; coastal dwellers who worked in fishing and salt-making earned large profits with little effort.

sentences.zh: 繇是不逞無賴盜販者眾，捕之急則起為盜賊。

translations.literal: Thus there were many insubordinate ruffians who smuggled salt illicitly; when pursuit was pressed hard they rose up as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Thus a large number of unruly smugglers appeared, and when the authorities pressed arrests too hard they turned into outright bandits.

sentences.zh: 江、淮間雖衣冠士人，狃於厚利，或以販鹽為事。

translations.literal: Even between the Yangtze and Huai, though gentry and scholars, accustomed to thick profit, sometimes took salt smuggling as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Even gentry between the Yangtze and Huai, lured by heavy profits, sometimes made their living smuggling salt.

sentences.zh: 江西則虔州地連廣南，而福建之汀州亦與虔接，虔鹽弗善，汀故不產鹽，二州民多盜販廣南鹽以射利。

translations.literal: In Jiangxi, Qian prefecture's territory adjoined Guangnan, and Fujian's Ting prefecture also bordered Qian; Qian salt was not good, and Ting originally did not produce salt — the people of the two prefectures mostly smuggled Guangnan salt to seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi, Qian prefecture bordered Guangnan and Ting prefecture in Fujian lay adjacent; with poor official salt in Qian and no local production in Ting, residents of both prefectures smuggled Guangnan salt for profit.

sentences.zh: 每歲秋冬，田事才畢，恒數十百為群，持甲兵旗鼓，往來虔、汀、漳、潮、循、梅、惠、廣八州之地。

translations.literal: Every year in autumn and winter, when field work had just finished, they constantly grouped in tens or hundreds, bearing armor, weapons, drums, and banners, traveling back and forth through the eight prefectures of Qian, Ting, Zhang, Chao, Xun, Mei, Hui, and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Each autumn and winter, as soon as the harvest ended, they formed bands of dozens or hundreds, armed and bearing banners, and roamed among the eight prefectures of Qian, Ting, Zhang, Chao, Xun, Mei, Hui, and Guang.

sentences.zh: 所至劫人穀帛，掠人婦女，與巡捕吏卒鬥格，至殺傷吏卒，則起為盜，依阻險要，捕不能得，或赦其罪招之。

translations.literal: Wherever they went they robbed people's grain and cloth, plundered women, and fought with patrol officers and soldiers; when they killed or wounded officers and soldiers they rose as bandits, relying on steep and strategic terrain so they could not be captured, or their crimes were pardoned to recruit them.
translations.idiomatic: They robbed grain and cloth, seized women, and fought patrol troops; once they killed officials they became full bandits, holding mountain passes where pursuers could not reach them — or the court pardoned them and brought them in.

sentences.zh: 歲月浸淫滋多，而州官糶鹽歲才及百萬斤。

translations.literal: As months and years gradually spread and multiplied, yet the prefectural officials' annual salt sales reached only one million jin.
translations.idiomatic: The problem grew year by year, while official salt sales in the prefecture amounted to only one million jin annually.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，廣東轉運使李敷、王繇請運廣州鹽於南雄州，以給虔、吉，未報，即運四百餘萬斤於南雄；

translations.literal: During Qingli, Guangdong transport commissioners Li Fu and Wang Yao requested transporting Guangzhou salt to Nanxiong prefecture to supply Qian and Ji; before a reply came, they immediately transported over 4,000,000 jin to Nanxiong;
translations.idiomatic: During Qingli, Guangdong transport commissioners Li Fu and Wang Yao asked to ship Guangzhou salt to Nanxiong to supply Qian and Ji; without waiting for approval they moved more than 4,000,000 jin there;

sentences.zh: 而江西轉運司不以為便，不往取。

translations.literal: but the Jiangxi transport commission did not consider it convenient and did not go to collect it.
translations.idiomatic: but the Jiangxi transport commission found the arrangement impractical and refused to collect the salt.

sentences.zh: 後三司戶部判官周湛等八人復請運廣鹽入虔州，江西亦請自具本錢取之。

translations.literal: Later the Three Departments revenue commissioner Zhou Zhan and eight others again requested transporting Guang salt into Qian prefecture; Jiangxi also requested to supply capital funds itself to take the salt.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou Zhan, a Three Departments revenue commissioner, and seven colleagues again proposed shipping Guang salt into Qian, and Jiangxi offered to pay the capital costs itself.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書屯田員外郎施元長等會議，皆請如湛等議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Director of Field Revenue Shi Yuanchang and others to confer; all requested acting according to Zhou Zhan's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Vice Director of Field Revenue Shi Yuanchang and others to meet, and all endorsed Zhou Zhan's plan.

sentences.zh: 而發運使許元以為不可，遂止。

translations.literal: But Consignment Commissioner Xu Yuan considered it impossible, and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Consignment Commissioner Xu Yuan objected, however, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐以來，或請商販廣南鹽入虔、汀，所過州縣收算；

translations.literal: Since Jiayou, some requested allowing merchants to trade Guangnan salt into Qian and Ting, with prefectures and counties along the route collecting transit duties;
translations.idiomatic: Since Jiayou various proposals circulated: let merchants carry Guangnan salt into Qian and Ting with transit fees at each stop;

sentences.zh: 或請放虔、汀、漳、循、梅、潮、惠七州鹽通商；

translations.literal: some requested releasing salt in the seven prefectures of Qian, Ting, Zhang, Xun, Mei, Chao, and Hui to open general trade;
translations.idiomatic: open salt trade entirely in the seven prefectures of Qian, Ting, Zhang, Xun, Mei, Chao, and Hui;

sentences.zh: 或謂第歲運淮南鹽七百萬斤至虔，二百萬斤至汀，民間足鹽，寇盜自息；

translations.literal: some said that merely transporting 7,000,000 jin of Huainan salt annually to Qian and 2,000,000 jin to Ting would suffice salt for the people and bandits would cease of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: simply ship 7,000,000 jin of Huainan salt yearly to Qian and 2,000,000 jin to Ting so the people would have enough salt and smuggling would die down;

sentences.zh: 或請官自置鋪役兵卒，運廣南、福建鹽至虔、汀州，論者不一。

translations.literal: some requested that the government establish its own shops, corvee labor, and soldiers to transport Guangnan and Fujian salt to Qian and Ting prefectures — the debaters were not of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: or have the state run shops and troops to haul Guangnan and Fujian salt to Qian and Ting — opinions remained divided.

sentences.zh: 先嘗遣職方員外郎黃炳乘傳會所屬監司及知州、通判議，謂虔州食淮南鹽已久，不可改，第損近歲所增官估，斤為錢四十，以十縣五等戶夏秋稅率百錢令糴鹽二斤，隨夏稅入錢償官。

translations.literal: Previously they had dispatched Field Works Vice Director Huang Bing by imperial courier to convene the supervising commissioners and the prefectural and circuit intendants to discuss; they said Qian had consumed Huainan salt for a long time and could not be changed, only reduce the recent years' increased official assessment to forty cash per jin, and order the five-grade households of ten counties, at a summer-autumn tax rate of one hundred cash, to purchase two jin of salt, repaying the government with summer-tax cash payments.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Field Works Vice Director Huang Bing had been sent by imperial courier to consult local commissioners and prefectural officials; they argued that Qian had long relied on Huainan salt and the supply should not be switched, but the recent price hike could be rolled back to forty cash per jin, with households in ten counties required to buy two jin per hundred cash of summer and autumn tax and repay the state through their tax payments.

sentences.zh: 繼命提點鑄錢沈扶覆視可否，扶等請選江西漕船團為十綱，以三班使臣部之，直取通、泰、楚都倉鹽。

translations.literal: Subsequently they ordered Mint Supervisor Shen Fu to review whether it was feasible; Fu and others requested selecting Jiangxi transport boats grouped into ten convoys, with third-rank commissioners to command them, taking salt directly from the central warehouses of Tong, Tai, and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Fu, the mint supervisor, was then told to reassess the plan; he proposed forming ten convoys from Jiangxi transport boats under third-rank commissioners, drawing salt straight from the Tong, Tai, and Chu central stores.

sentences.zh: 詔用炳等策，然歲才增糶六十餘萬斤。

translations.literal: An edict adopted Huang Bing's plan, yet annually it increased salt sales by only over 600,000 jin.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Huang Bing's scheme, but annual sales rose by only a little over 600,000 jin.

sentences.zh: 江西提點刑獄蔡挺製置鹽事，乃令民首納私藏兵械給巡捕吏卒，而販黃魚籠挾鹽不及二十斤、徒不及五人、不以甲兵自隨者，止輸算勿捕。

translations.literal: Jiangxi judicial intendant Cai Ting took charge of salt affairs; he ordered the people to turn in privately stored weapons first and give them to patrol officers and soldiers, while those selling yellow fish in baskets with less than twenty jin of salt concealed, with fewer than five companions, and not bearing armor and weapons themselves, were only to pay transit duties and not be arrested.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi judicial intendant Cai Ting took over salt policy, he required civilians to surrender hidden weapons to patrol troops; smugglers carrying less than twenty jin of salt in fish baskets, with fewer than five men and no arms, had only to pay transit fees and were not arrested.

sentences.zh: 淮南既團新綱漕鹽，挺增為十二綱，綱二十五艘，鎖栿至州乃發。

translations.literal: Since Huainan had already grouped new convoys for salt transport, Ting increased them to twelve convoys, twenty-five vessels per convoy, sealed and bound until reaching the prefecture before release.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan had already organized new salt convoys; Ting expanded the system to twelve convoys of twenty-five boats each, kept sealed until they reached the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 輸官有餘，以畀漕舟吏卒，官復以半賈取之，繇是減侵盜之弊，鹽遂差善。

translations.literal: When surplus was delivered to the government it was given to transport-boat officers and soldiers, and the government again took it back at half price; thus the abuse of embezzlement was reduced and the salt became somewhat better.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus salt delivered to the state was allotted to boat crews, whom the government then bought it back from at half price; this cut down theft and improved salt quality.

sentences.zh: 又損糶價，歲課視舊增至三百餘萬斤，乃罷炳等議所率糴鹽錢。

translations.literal: He also reduced the sale price; annual revenue compared with the old amount increased to over 3,000,000 jin, and then the compulsory salt-purchase money from Huang Bing's proposal was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He cut sale prices as well, raising annual receipts to more than 3,000,000 jin over the old level, and ended the mandatory salt-purchase levy tied to Huang Bing's plan.

sentences.zh: 異時，汀州人欲販鹽，輒先伐鼓山谷中，召願從者與期日，率常得數十百人已上，與俱行。

translations.literal: Formerly, when people in Ting prefecture wished to smuggle salt, they would first beat drums in mountain valleys, summon willing followers and set a date, usually gathering several tens or hundreds or more, and travel together.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times Ting smugglers would drum in the hills to rally recruits and set a rendezvous, routinely mustering scores or even hundreds before setting out together.

sentences.zh: 至是，州縣督責耆保，有伐鼓者輒捕送，盜販者稍稍畏縮。

translations.literal: At this time prefectures and counties supervised and held responsible the elders and baojia leaders; whoever beat drums was immediately arrested and sent away, and smugglers gradually grew fearful and shrank back.
translations.idiomatic: Now prefectures and counties pressed village elders and baojia heads to act: anyone who beat the drum was arrested at once, and smugglers slowly pulled back.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以挺為能，留之江西，積數年乃徙。

translations.literal: The court considered Ting capable, kept him in Jiangxi, and only transferred him after several years had accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Ting effective and kept him in Jiangxi for several years before moving him elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 久之，江西鹽皆團綱運致如虔州焉。

translations.literal: After a long time, all Jiangxi salt was convoy-transported and delivered just as in Qian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In time all Jiangxi salt was shipped in convoys on the Qian model.

sentences.zh: 初，荊湖亦病鹽惡，且歲漕常不足，治平二年，才及二十五萬餘石。

translations.literal: Initially Jing-Hu also suffered from poor salt quality, and annual transport was often insufficient; in the second year of Zhiping it reached only over 250,000 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Jing-Hu likewise struggled with bad salt and chronic shortfalls in transport; in the second year of Zhiping deliveries totaled barely 250,000 piculs.

sentences.zh: 三年，撥淮西二十四綱及傭客舟載鹽以往，是歲運及四十萬石。

translations.literal: In the third year they allocated Huixi twenty-four convoys and hired passenger boats to carry salt thither; that year transport reached 400,000 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The third year they assigned twenty-four Huixi convoys plus hired merchant vessels, and shipments that year reached 400,000 piculs.

sentences.zh: 四年，至五十三萬餘石。

translations.literal: In the fourth year it reached over 530,000 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth year deliveries rose to more than 530,000 piculs.

sentences.zh: 慶曆初，判戶部勾院王琪言：「天禧初，嘗以荊湖鹽估高，詔斤減三錢或二錢，自後利入寢損。

translations.literal: Early in Qingli, Wang Qi of the Revenue Review Office said: "Early in Tiansi, because Jing-Hu salt assessments were high, an edict reduced the price per jin by three or two cash; after that revenue gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingli, Wang Qi of the Revenue Review Office reported: "At the start of Tiansi, Jing-Hu salt prices were cut by two or three cash per jin because assessments were too high, and receipts have steadily fallen since.

sentences.zh: 請復舊估，可歲增緡錢四萬。」

translations.literal: I request restoring the old assessment; this can annually increase revenue by 40,000 strings of cash."
translations.idiomatic: Restore the old price and revenue should rise by 40,000 strings a year."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 治平中，淮南轉運使李復圭、張芻、蘇頌，三司度支判官韓縝，相繼請減淮南鹽價，然卒不果行。

translations.literal: During Zhiping, Huainan transport commissioners Li Fugui, Zhang Chu, and Su Song, and Three Departments fiscal commissioner Han Zong successively requested reducing Huainan salt prices, yet in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhiping, Huainan transport commissioners Li Fugui, Zhang Chu, and Su Song, together with fiscal commissioner Han Zong of the Three Departments, repeatedly asked to cut Huainan salt prices, but none of the proposals took effect.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，江西鹽課不登，三年，提點刑獄張頡言：「虔州官鹽鹵濕雜惡，輕不及斤，而價至四十七錢。

translations.literal: Early in Xining, Jiangxi salt revenue failed to meet its quota; in the third year judicial intendant Zhang Ji said: "Official salt in Qian was briny, damp, adulterated, and poor — it weighed less than a full jin yet cost as much as forty-seven cash.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining Jiangxi salt receipts fell short; in the third year judicial intendant Zhang Ji reported: "Qian's official salt was wet, adulterated, and underweight, yet sold for forty-seven cash a jin.

sentences.zh: 嶺南盜販入虔，以斤半當一斤，純白不雜，賣錢二十，以故虔人盡食嶺南鹽。

translations.literal: Smuggled salt from Lingnan entered Qian; a jin and a half counted as one jin, pure white and unadulterated, selling for twenty cash — for this reason the people of Qian all ate Lingnan salt.
translations.idiomatic: Smuggled Lingnan salt offered a jin and a half for the price of one jin of pure white salt at twenty cash, so Qian residents ate nothing but Lingnan salt.

sentences.zh: 乃議稍減虔鹽價，更擇壯舟，團為十綱，以使臣部押。

translations.literal: They therefore discussed slightly reducing Qian salt prices, selecting stout boats anew, grouping them into ten convoys, and having commissioners command and escort them.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed trimming Qian's official price, reassigning sturdy boats into ten convoys under imperial commissioners.

sentences.zh: 後蔡挺以贛江道險，議令鹽船三歲一易，仍以鹽純雜增虧為綱官、舟人殿最，鹽課遂敷，盜販衰止。

translations.literal: Later Cai Ting, because the Gan River route was perilous, proposed that salt boats be replaced every three years, and still used the purity, adulteration, surplus, and deficit of salt as the basis for ranking convoy officers and boatmen; salt revenue then met its quota and smuggling declined and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ting later argued that the Gan River route was treacherous and salt boats should be replaced every three years; convoy officers and crews would be graded on salt purity and losses, which brought receipts back up and curbed smuggling.

sentences.zh: 自挺去，法十廢五六，請復之便。」

translations.literal: Since Ting departed, five or six tenths of the law fell into disuse; I request restoring it as expedient."
translations.idiomatic: Since Ting left, five or six tenths of his measures had lapsed; restoring them would be advisable."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 仍定歲運淮鹽十二綱至虔州。

translations.literal: It also fixed annual transport of twelve Huainan salt convoys to Qian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It also set twelve annual Huainan salt convoys for Qian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及章惇察訪湖南，符本路提點刑獄朱初平措置般運廣鹽，添額出賣，然未及行。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun inspected Hunan, he ordered this circuit's judicial intendant Zhu Chuping to arrange transport of Guang salt, increase the quota, and sell it — yet it had not yet been implemented.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun toured Hunan he told judicial intendant Zhu Chuping to organize Guang salt shipments and raise sales quotas, but the plan was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，惇既參政，有郟亶者，邪險銳進，素為惇所喜，迎合惇意，推仿湖南之法，乞運廣鹽於江西。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng, after Dun had entered the administration, there was a Jia Dan — devious, ruthless, and aggressively ambitious, long favored by Dun — who catered to Dun's intent, extrapolated and imitated the Hunan method, and requested transporting Guang salt to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng, with Zhang Dun already in power, a protégé named Jia Dan — cunning and ruthlessly ambitious — flattered him by extending the Hunan model and asking to ship Guang salt into Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 即遣蹇周輔往江西相度。

translations.literal: They immediately dispatched Jian Zhoufu to Jiangxi to survey and assess.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Zhoufu was immediately sent to Jiangxi to survey the plan.

sentences.zh: 周輔承望惇意，奏言：「虔州運路險遠，淮鹽至者不能多，人苦淡食，廣東鹽不得輒通，盜販公行。

translations.literal: Zhoufu, deferring to Dun's intent, memorialized: "Qian's transport route was perilous and distant; Huainan salt that arrived could not be plentiful, and people suffered from bland food; Guangdong salt could not be freely passed through, and smuggling went on openly.
translations.idiomatic: Currying favor with Zhang Dun, Zhoufu reported: "Qian's route was long and dangerous, so little Huainan salt arrived; people lacked salt, Guangdong salt was barred, and smuggling flourished openly.

sentences.zh: 淮鹽官以九錢致一斤，若運廣鹽盡會其費，減淮鹽一錢，而其鹽更善，運路無阻。

translations.literal: Official Huainan salt cost nine cash to obtain one jin; if Guang salt were transported and all costs totaled, Huainan salt could be reduced by one cash, yet its salt would be better and the transport route unobstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Official Huainan salt cost nine cash per jin to deliver; Guang salt at equal total cost could replace it with a one-cash reduction, better quality, and no transport obstacles.

sentences.zh: 請罷運淮鹽，通般廣鹽一千萬斤於江西虔州、南安軍，復均淮鹽六百一十六萬斤於洪、吉、筠、袁、撫、臨江、建昌、興國軍，以補舊額。」

translations.literal: I request abolishing Huainan salt transport, opening general transport of 10,000,000 jin of Guang salt to Qian prefecture and Nan'an Army in Jiangxi, and again distributing 6,160,000 jin of Huainan salt among Hong, Ji, Jun, Yuan, Fu, Linjiang, Jianchang, and Xingguo Army to make up the old quota."
translations.idiomatic: Stop shipping Huainan salt and move 10,000,000 jin of Guang salt to Qian and Nan'an in Jiangxi, while reallocating 6,160,000 jin of Huainan salt among Hong, Ji, Jun, Yuan, Fu, Linjiang, Jianchang, and Xingguo to cover the old quota."

sentences.zh: 詔周輔立法以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhoufu to draft laws and report.
translations.idiomatic: The court told Zhoufu to draft regulations and report back.

sentences.zh: 周輔具鹽法並總目條上，大率峻剝於民，民被其害。

translations.literal: Zhoufu submitted the complete salt law together with summary articles; on the whole it harshly extracted from the people, and the people suffered its harm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhoufu submitted the full salt code and summary articles, which on the whole squeezed the populace harshly.

sentences.zh: 舊，江西鹽場許民買撲，周輔悉籍於官賣之。

translations.literal: Formerly Jiangxi salterns allowed the people to bid for leases; Zhoufu registered them all under government control and sold the salt.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Jiangxi salterns could be leased by private bid; Zhoufu placed them all under direct state sale.

sentences.zh: 遂以周輔遙領提舉江西、廣東鹽事，即司農寺置局。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhoufu was appointed from afar to supervise Jiangxi and Guangdong salt affairs, and a bureau was established in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhoufu was then put in remote charge of Jiangxi and Guangdong salt policy, with a bureau set up in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四年，周輔改漕河北。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zhoufu was transferred to transport duties in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth year Zhoufu was reassigned to Hebei transport duties.

sentences.zh: 明年，提舉常平劉誼言道途洶洶，以賣鹽為患。

translations.literal: The next year Ever-Normal Granary intendant Liu Yi said the roads were in an uproar and salt sales had become an affliction.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Ever-Normal Granary intendant Liu Yi reported widespread unrest caused by forced salt sales.

sentences.zh: 詔江東提點刑獄範峋體量，未報，誼坐言役法等事罷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jiangdong judicial intendant Fan Xun to investigate and assess; before a report came, Yi was dismissed on account of speaking about corvee law and other matters.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdong judicial intendant Fan Xun was ordered to investigate; before he reported, Liu Yi was removed after criticizing the corvee laws.

sentences.zh: 及峋奏至，但以州縣違法塞詔，竟無更張。

translations.literal: When Xun's memorial arrived, it only said that prefectures and counties had violated the law and blocked the edict; in the end there was no change.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Xun's report arrived it blamed local officials for blocking the edict, and no policy change followed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，周輔奏：「虔州、南安軍推行鹽法方半年，已收息十四萬緡。」

translations.literal: Before long Zhoufu memorialized: "Qian prefecture and Nan'an Army had implemented the salt law for only half a year and had already collected profit of 140,000 strings of cash."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhoufu reported: "Qian and Nan'an had run the new salt law for only half a year and already cleared 140,000 strings in profit.

sentences.zh: 自以為功。

translations.literal: He himself regarded it as an achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He counted it as his achievement.

sentences.zh: 詔命發運副使李琮體訪利害，琮知周輔方被獎用，止謂鹽法宜變通而已，不敢斥言其害。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Commissioner of Consignment Transport Li Cong to investigate benefits and harms on the ground; Cong knew Zhoufu was then being rewarded and employed, and only said the salt law ought to be adjusted — he did not dare openly denounce its harm.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Li Cong was told to assess the policy on the ground; knowing Zhoufu was in favor, he merely suggested minor adjustments and did not denounce the harm openly.

sentences.zh: 六年，周輔為戶部侍郎，復奏湖南郴、道州鄰接韶、連，可以通運廣鹽數百萬，卻均舊賣淮鹽於潭、衡、永、全、邵等州，並準江西、廣東見法，仍舉郟亶初議，郴、全、道三州亦賣廣鹽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zhoufu became Vice Minister of Revenue and again memorialized that Hunan's Chen and Dao prefectures bordered Shao and Lian and could open transport of several million jin of Guang salt, while instead distributing the old Huainan salt sales among Tan, Heng, Yong, Quan, Shao, and other prefectures; all would follow the current methods of Jiangxi and Guangdong, still citing Jia Dan's original proposal — Chen, Quan, and Dao prefectures would also sell Guang salt.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth year, now Vice Minister of Revenue, Zhoufu proposed extending Guang salt shipments of several million jin into Chen and Dao in Hunan, which border Shao and Lian, while reallocating former Huainan salt sales among Tan, Heng, Yong, Quan, and Shao under the Jiangxi-Guangdong model Jia Dan had first suggested; Chen, Quan, and Dao would sell Guang salt as well.

sentences.zh: 詔委提舉常平張士澄、轉運判官陳偲措置。

translations.literal: An edict entrusted Ever-Normal Granary intendant Zhang Shicheng and transport vice commissioner Chen Si to arrange matters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng, intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries, and transport vice commissioner Chen Si were ordered to implement the plan.

sentences.zh: 明年，士澄等具條約來上，詔施行之，額利增加，一方騷然。

translations.literal: The next year Shicheng and others submitted detailed regulations; an edict ordered implementation, the quota profit increased, and the whole region was in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they submitted detailed regulations, the court put them into effect, quotas rose, and the region erupted in unrest.

sentences.zh: 於時淮西亦推行周輔鹽法，發運使蔣之奇奏立知州、通判、鹽事官賞罰，下戶部著為令。

translations.literal: At that time Huixi also implemented Zhoufu's salt law; Consignment Commissioner Jiang Zhiqi memorialized establishing rewards and punishments for prefects, vice prefects, and salt officials, and the Revenue Ministry issued it as a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Huixi adopted Zhoufu's salt law as well; consignment commissioner Jiang Zhiqi asked for reward-and-punishment rules for prefects, vice prefects, and salt officials, which the Revenue Ministry codified.

sentences.zh: 紹聖三年，發運司言淮南亭戶貧瘠，官賦本錢六十四萬緡，皆倚辦諸路，以故不時至，民無所得錢，必舉倍稱之息。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng the consignment transport directorate reported that Huainan saltern households were poor and depleted; the official capital funds of 640,000 strings of cash all depended on fulfillment by the various circuits, and for this reason they did not arrive on time; the people received no cash and inevitably borrowed at double the normal interest.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shaosheng the consignment directorate reported that Huainan saltern households were destitute: the state's 640,000 strings in capital funds relied on circuit contributions that arrived late, leaving saltern families without cash and forcing them to borrow at usurious rates.

sentences.zh: 欲以糴本錢十萬緡給之，不足，畀以憑由，即欲質於官，與平之七，而蠲其息，鹽本集，復給其三分，憑由毀棄。

translations.literal: They wished to give 100,000 strings of cash in purchase capital; if insufficient, issue certificates of credit so they could pawn them with the government at seven-tenths of fair value, remit the interest, and when salt capital was collected restore the remaining three-tenths and destroy the certificates.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed advancing 100,000 strings in purchase capital, or issuing pawn certificates redeemable at seventy percent of face value with interest waived; once salt capital was collected the remaining thirty percent would be paid and the certificates destroyed.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，蔡京議更鹽法，乃言東南鹽本或闕，滯於客販，請增給度牒及給封樁坊場錢通三十萬緡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning, Cai Jing discussed changing the salt law and said southeastern salt capital was sometimes deficient and stagnated among traveling merchants; he requested an additional grant of ordination certificates and sealed-reserve market funds totaling 300,000 strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongning, Cai Jing proposed revising the salt law, noting that southeastern salt capital sometimes ran short and sat idle among merchant traders; he asked for an extra 300,000 strings in ordination certificates and sealed-reserve market funds.

sentences.zh: 並列七條：一、許客用私船運致，仍嚴立輒逾疆至夾帶私鹽之禁；

translations.literal: He also listed seven articles: First, permit merchants to transport using private boats, while strictly establishing prohibitions against casually crossing boundaries or smuggling private salt along with it;
translations.idiomatic: He added seven provisions: first, allow merchants to ship on private vessels but strictly forbid crossing boundaries or carrying illicit salt;

sentences.zh: 二、鹽場官吏概量不平或支鹽失倫次者，論以徒；

translations.literal: Second, saltern officials who measured unfairly with the scoop or disbursed salt out of proper order were to be sentenced to penal servitude;
translations.idiomatic: second, saltern officials who short-measured or issued salt out of turn would face penal servitude;

sentences.zh: 三、鹽商所繇官司、場務、堰閘、津渡等輒加苛留者，如上法；

translations.literal: Third, wherever salt merchants passed through — government offices, market posts, weirs, locks, ferry crossings, and the like — those who arbitrarily added harsh detentions were punished by the same law;
translations.idiomatic: third, officials at offices, market posts, locks, and ferries along merchant routes who detained salt shipments would be punished the same way;

sentences.zh: 四、禁命吏、蔭家、貢士、胥史為賈區請鹽；

translations.literal: Fourth, prohibit appointed clerks, yin privilege families, tribute scholars, and petty officials from requesting salt on behalf of merchant zones;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, ban appointed clerks, yin families, tribute scholars, and petty officials from procuring salt for merchant zones;

sentences.zh: 五、議貸亭戶；

translations.literal: Fifth, discuss lending to saltern households;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, provide loans to saltern households;

sentences.zh: 六、鹽價大低者議增之；

translations.literal: Sixth, where salt prices were greatly low, discuss increasing them;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, raise prices where they had fallen too low;

sentences.zh: 七、令措置官博盡利害以聞。

translations.literal: Seventh, order arranging officials to exhaustively report benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: seventh, require arranging officials to report fully on costs and benefits.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔鹽舟力勝錢勿輸，用絕阻遏，且許舟行越次取疾，官綱等舟輒攔阻者坐之。

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered that salt boats need not pay capacity-based transit fees, to cut off obstruction; moreover boats were permitted to travel out of turn to go faster, and official convoy boats or the like that arbitrarily blocked and detained them were to be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the court exempted salt boats from capacity transit fees to prevent holdups, allowed them to pass out of turn for speed, and penalized official convoys that blocked them.

sentences.zh: 遂變鈔法，置買鈔所於榷貨務。

translations.literal: Thereupon the certificate law was changed, and certificate purchase offices were established at the monopoly goods office.
translations.idiomatic: The certificate system was then revised and purchase offices set up at the monopoly goods office.

sentences.zh: 凡以鈔至者，並以末鹽、乳香、茶鈔並東北一分及官告、度牒、雜物等換給。

translations.literal: All who arrived with certificates were alike given exchange for powdered salt certificates, frankincense, tea certificates together with the northeastern one-tenth portion, as well as official appointments, ordination certificates, and miscellaneous goods.
translations.idiomatic: Certificate holders could exchange them for powdered-salt certificates, frankincense, tea certificates with the northeastern one-tenth share, official appointments, ordination certificates, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 末鹽鈔換易五分，餘以雜物，而舊鈔止許易末鹽、官告。

translations.literal: Powdered salt certificates could be exchanged for five-tenths; the remainder was in miscellaneous goods, while old certificates were permitted exchange only for powdered salt and official appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Powdered-salt certificates could be redeemed fifty percent in kind and the rest in miscellaneous goods; old certificates could be exchanged only for powdered salt and official appointments.

sentences.zh: 仍以十分率之，止聽算三分，其七分兼新鈔。

translations.literal: Still calculating by tenths, only three-tenths were permitted as cash settlement; the remaining seven-tenths had to include new certificates.
translations.idiomatic: On a ten-part basis only three parts could be settled in cash; the other seven had to include new certificates.

sentences.zh: 定民間買鈔之價，以抑豪強，以平邊糴。

translations.literal: The price for the people to buy certificates was fixed, to suppress powerful magnates and to stabilize border grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: Certificate purchase prices were fixed to curb powerful speculators and stabilize border grain procurement.

sentences.zh: 在河北買者，率百緡毋得下五千，東南末鹽鈔毋得下十千，陝西鹽鈔毋得下五千五百，私減者坐徒徙之罪，官吏留難、文鈔展限等條皆備。
