translations.literal: For buyers in Hebei, per hundred strings none could fall below 5,000; for southeastern powdered salt certificates none below 10,000; for Shaanxi salt certificates none below 5,500; private reduction incurred penal servitude or exile; provisions were complete for officials' obstruction, extending certificate deadlines, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei the floor was 5,000 per hundred strings; southeastern powdered-salt certificates could not fall below 10,000; Shaanxi salt certificates not below 5,500; unauthorized discounts brought penal servitude or exile, with full rules against official obstruction and deadline extensions.

sentences.zh: 四年，又以算請鹽價輕重不等，載定六路鹽價，舊價二十錢以上皆遞增以十錢，四十五者如舊；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because cash-settlement salt prices were unequal in weight, salt prices for the six circuits were fixed in the records; old prices of twenty cash or more were all progressively increased by ten cash, while forty-five cash remained as before;
translations.idiomatic: The fourth year, because cash-settlement salt prices varied, the six circuits' prices were standardized: former prices of twenty cash or more rose by ten, while forty-five cash stayed unchanged;

sentences.zh: 算請東南末鹽，願折以金銀、物帛者聽其便。

translations.literal: For cash settlement to request southeastern powdered salt, those wishing to convert to gold, silver, or cloth and silk were permitted as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: those settling in cash for southeastern powdered salt could convert payment to gold, silver, or cloth at their option.

sentences.zh: 而亭戶貸錢，舊輸息二分者蠲之。

translations.literal: As for loans to saltern households, the old two-percent interest payment was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Interest on loans to saltern households, formerly two percent, was waived.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔算請不貼納見錢，以十分率之，毋過二分。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict ordered that cash settlement need not include supplementary cash payment; calculating by tenths, it must not exceed two-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth year the court ruled that cash settlements need not include supplementary cash payments, capped at two-tenths on a ten-part basis.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，乃令算請東南末鹽貼輸及帶舊鈔如見條外，更許帶日前貼輸三分鹽鈔，輸四分者帶二分，五分者帶三分。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan it was ordered that beyond cash settlement for southeastern powdered salt with supplementary payment and carrying old certificates according to current articles, it was further permitted to carry prior-day supplementary three-tenths salt certificates; those paying four-tenths could carry two-tenths, and those paying five-tenths could carry three-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daguan, beyond existing rules on supplementary payments and old certificates for southeastern powdered salt, holders could also include prior supplementary three-tenths salt certificates: four-tenths payers could add two-tenths, five-tenths payers three-tenths.

sentences.zh: 後又貼輸四分者帶三分，五分者帶四分，而東南鹽並收見緡換請新鈔者，如四分五分法貼輸。

translations.literal: Later those paying four-tenths supplementary could carry three-tenths, and those paying five-tenths could carry four-tenths; moreover for southeastern salt, those who paid cash strings to exchange for new certificates followed the four-tenths and five-tenths method for supplementary payment.
translations.idiomatic: Later four-tenths supplementary payers could add three-tenths and five-tenths payers four-tenths; cash payers exchanging for new southeastern salt certificates followed the same supplementary ratios.

sentences.zh: 其換請新鈔及見錢算東南末鹽，如不帶六等舊鈔者，聽先給；

translations.literal: For those exchanging for new certificates and using cash to settle for southeastern powdered salt, if they did not carry old certificates of the six grades, they were permitted to receive salt first;
translations.idiomatic: Those exchanging for new certificates or paying cash for southeastern powdered salt without six-grade old certificates could receive salt first;

sentences.zh: 如止帶五等舊鈔，其給鹽之敘，在崇寧四年十月前所帶不貼輸舊鈔之上。

translations.literal: if they carried only five-grade old certificates, the order of salt disbursement ranked above the old certificates without supplementary payment carried before the tenth month of the fourth year of Chongning.
translations.idiomatic: if they carried only five-grade old certificates, they ranked above holders of non-supplementary old certificates from before the tenth month of Chongning's fourth year.

sentences.zh: 六等者，謂貼三、貼四、貼五、當十鈔、並河北公據、免貼納錢是也。

translations.literal: The six grades meant supplementary three-tenths, supplementary four-tenths, supplementary five-tenths, ten-for-one certificates, together with Hebei public vouchers and exemption from supplementary payment.
translations.idiomatic: The six grades were supplementary three-, four-, and five-tenths certificates, ten-for-one certificates, Hebei public vouchers, and certificates exempt from supplementary payment.

sentences.zh: 時鈔法紛易，公私交弊。

translations.literal: At the time the certificate law changed repeatedly, and public and private interests alike suffered harm.
translations.idiomatic: Certificate rules shifted constantly, harming both government and private trade.

sentences.zh: 四年，侍御史毛注言：「崇寧以來，鹽法頓易元豐舊制，不許諸路以官船回載為轉運司之利，許人任便用鈔請鹽，般載於所指州縣販易，而出賣州縣用為課額。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Remonstrance Bureau Attendant Censor Mao Zhu said: "Since Chongning the salt law suddenly changed the old Yuanfeng system, no longer permitting the circuits to use official boats for return cargo as profit for the transport commission, permitting people freely to use certificates to request salt, transport it to designated prefectures and counties for trade, and using sales by prefectures and counties as revenue quotas.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth year, censor Mao Zhu reported: "Since Chongning the salt law abruptly replaced Yuanfeng practice: circuits could no longer profit from return cargo on official boats; merchants could freely use certificates to claim salt, ship it to assigned counties for sale, and those sales became local revenue quotas.

sentences.zh: 提舉鹽事司苛責郡縣，以賣鹽多寡為官吏殿最，一有循職養民不忍侵克，則指為沮法，必重奏劾譴黜，州縣孰不望風畏威，競為刻虐？

translations.literal: The salt affairs intendant office harshly held prefectures and counties responsible, using the amount of salt sold as the basis for ranking officials; whenever one conscientiously nurtured the people and could not bear to encroach and extract, they were denounced as obstructing the law and inevitably heavily memorialized, impeached, and dismissed — which prefecture or county would not look to the wind and fear authority, competing to be harsh and cruel?
translations.idiomatic: Salt intendant offices pressured counties on sales volume as the basis for official rankings; any magistrate who refused to squeeze the people was accused of obstructing policy, impeached, and removed — so who would not compete in cruelty?

sentences.zh: 由是東南諸州每縣三等以上戶，俱以物產高下，勒認鹽數之多寡。

translations.literal: Thus in every prefecture of the southeast, households of the third grade and above in each county were all, according to the high or low level of their property and produce, compelled to acknowledge how much salt they must take.
translations.idiomatic: Across the southeast, third-grade households and above in every county were forced to accept salt quotas based on their wealth and output.

sentences.zh: 上戶歲限有至千緡，第三等末戶不下三五十貫，籍為定數，使依數販易，以足歲額；

translations.literal: For upper-grade households the annual quota reached as much as 1,000 strings; for lowest third-grade households it was no less than thirty or fifty strings of cash; registered as fixed numbers, they were made to trade accordingly to meet the annual quota;
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households faced annual quotas up to 1,000 strings; even the lowest third-grade households owed at least thirty or fifty strings, fixed by register and enforced to meet yearly targets;

sentences.zh: 稍或愆期，鞭撻隨之。

translations.literal: if they were even slightly overdue, flogging followed.
translations.idiomatic: any delay brought flogging.

sentences.zh: 一縣歲額有三五萬緡，今用為常額，實為害之大者。」

translations.literal: A single county's annual quota was thirty or fifty thousand strings; now used as a standing quota, this was in truth the greatest harm."
translations.idiomatic: A county's annual quota could reach thirty or fifty thousand strings, now fixed as a permanent levy — this is the gravest harm."

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He added:

sentences.zh: 「朝廷自昔謹三路之備，糧儲豐溢，其術非他，惟鈔法流通，上下交信。

translations.literal: "Since ancient times the court has been careful about preparedness in the three circuits; grain stores were abundant and overflowing — the method was nothing else but circulation of the certificate law and mutual trust between upper and lower.
translations.idiomatic: "The court has long guarded preparedness in the three frontier circuits, keeping grain stores full — and the method was nothing other than circulating certificates so that state and merchants trusted one another.

sentences.zh: 東南末鹽錢為河北之備，東北鹽為河東之備，解地鹽為陝西之備，其錢並積於京師，隨所積多寡給鈔於三路。

translations.literal: Revenue from southeastern powdered salt served as provision for Hebei, northeastern salt for Hedong, Jie-region salt for Shaanxi; the funds were all accumulated at the capital, and certificates were issued to the three circuits according to how much had accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Southeastern powdered salt revenue backed Hebei's frontier stores, northeastern salt backed Hedong's, and Jie-region salt backed Shaanxi's; all proceeds pooled at the capital, and the three circuits received certificates in proportion to what had been amassed.

sentences.zh: 如河北糧草鈔至京，並支見錢，號飛鈔法；

translations.literal: When Hebei grain-and-fodder certificates reached the capital, cash was paid in full — this was called the flying certificates method;
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei grain-and-fodder certificates arrived at the capital, they were redeemed entirely in hard cash — the flying certificates method;

sentences.zh: 河東三路至京，半支見錢，半支銀、綢、絹；

translations.literal: When Hedong's three circuits reached the capital, half was paid in cash and half in silver, silk gauze, and silk;
translations.idiomatic: Certificates from Hedong's three circuits were redeemed at the capital half in cash and half in silver, gauze, and silk;

sentences.zh: 陝西解鹽鈔則支請解鹽，或有泛給鈔，亦以京師錢支給。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Jie-salt certificates were redeemed for Jie salt; if certificates were issued indiscriminately, payment still came from capital funds.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Jie-salt certificates were exchanged for Jie salt; even when certificates were issued broadly, the capital treasury still paid them out.

sentences.zh: 為錢積於京師，鈔行於三路，至則給錢，不復滯留。

translations.literal: Because money accumulated at the capital and certificates circulated in the three circuits, upon arrival cash was paid and nothing lingered.
translations.idiomatic: Cash pooled at the capital while certificates moved through the three circuits; on arrival they were paid out at once, with no delay.

sentences.zh: 當時商旅皆悅，爭運糧草，入於邊郡。

translations.literal: At the time merchants were all pleased and competed to transport grain and fodder into border prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants welcomed the arrangement and competed to haul grain and fodder into the frontier prefectures.

sentences.zh: 商賈既通，物價亦平；

translations.literal: With commerce flowing, prices also stabilized;
translations.idiomatic: Trade opened up, and prices steadied;

sentences.zh: 官司上下，無有二價，斗米止百餘錢，束草不過三十；

translations.literal: Official and private prices were alike with no second price; a dou of rice was only a bit over one hundred cash, a bundle of fodder no more than thirty;
translations.idiomatic: Official and market prices matched; a dou of rice cost barely over a hundred cash, a bundle of fodder no more than thirty;

sentences.zh: 邊境倉廩，所在盈滿。

translations.literal: Border granaries everywhere overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier storehouses stood full wherever one looked.

sentences.zh: 自崇寧來鈔法屢更，人不敢信，京師無見錢之積，而給鈔數倍於昔年。

translations.literal: Since Chongning the certificate law had changed repeatedly; people dared not trust it; the capital held no accumulated cash, yet certificates issued ran several times the volume of former years.
translations.idiomatic: From the Chongning era onward the certificate system changed again and again until no one trusted it; the capital had no cash reserves, yet issued several times as many certificates as before.

sentences.zh: 鈔至京師，無錢可給，遂至鈔直十不得一。

translations.literal: When certificates reached the capital there was no cash to pay, until a certificate's value was less than one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Certificates arriving at the capital found no cash to redeem them, until each was worth less than a tenth of its face value.

sentences.zh: 邊郡無人入中，糴買不敷，乃以銀絹、見錢品搭文鈔，為糴買之直。

translations.literal: No one delivered goods at the border prefectures; procurement fell short; silver, silk, and cash were graded and mixed with paper certificates as the procurement price.
translations.idiomatic: Border counties received no deliveries and could not meet procurement quotas, so silver, silk, cash, and paper certificates were graded and blended to set the purchase price.

sentences.zh: 民間中糴，不復會算鈔直，惟計銀絹、見錢，須至高抬糧草之價，以就虛數。

translations.literal: Private deliverers no longer reckoned certificate value, counting only silver, silk, and cash; grain and fodder prices had to be greatly raised to meet fictitious totals.
translations.idiomatic: Private suppliers stopped counting certificate value and priced only in silver, silk, and cash, forcing grain and fodder prices sharply upward to satisfy inflated quotas.

sentences.zh: 致使官價幾倍於民間，斗米有至四百，束草不下百三十餘錢，軍儲不得不闕，財用不得不匱。

translations.literal: Thus official prices became several times those of the people; a dou of rice reached four hundred, a bundle of fodder no less than one hundred thirty-odd cash; military stores necessarily fell short and revenues necessarily grew exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Official prices rose to several times market rates; rice reached four hundred cash per dou and fodder at least a hundred thirty per bundle; military reserves ran dry and the treasury emptied.

sentences.zh: 如解鹽鈔每紙六千，今可直三千，商旅凡入東南末鹽鈔，乃以見錢四分、鹽引六分，榷貨務惟得七十千之入，而東南支鹽，官直百千，則鹽本已暗有所損矣。

translations.literal: For example, Jie-salt certificates were six thousand per sheet but now worth only three thousand; whenever merchants submitted southeastern powdered salt certificates, they paid four-tenths in cash and six-tenths in salt warrants; the monopoly goods office received only seventy thousand in revenue, yet southeastern salt paid out at an official rate of one hundred thousand — so the salt capital was secretly diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Jie-salt certificates once worth six thousand each now fetched three thousand; merchants buying southeastern powdered salt certificates paid forty percent cash and sixty percent in salt warrants, yielding the monopoly goods office only seventy thousand while southeastern salt was issued at the official hundred-thousand rate — a hidden loss on salt capital.

sentences.zh: 臣謂鈔法不循復熙、豐，則物價無由可平，邊儲無由可積，方今大計，無急於此。

translations.literal: Your subject says that unless the certificate law is restored along Xi-Feng lines, prices cannot be stabilized nor border stores accumulated; among present great plans nothing is more urgent than this.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that unless the certificate system is restored to the Xi-Feng model, prices will not stabilize and frontier reserves will not rebuild — no policy today is more urgent.

sentences.zh: 薛向昔講究於嘉祐中，行之未幾，穀價遽損，邊備有餘，逮及熙、豐，其法始備。

translations.literal: Xue Xiang once studied the matter in the Jiayou era; shortly after implementation grain prices fell sharply and border preparedness had surplus; by the Xi-Feng era the method was fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiang had worked out the system in the Jiayou period; within a short time grain prices dropped and frontier stores overflowed; by the Xi-Feng years the method was fully in place.

sentences.zh: 比年榷貨務不顧鈔法屢變，有誤邊計，惟冀貼納見錢，專買東南鹽鈔，圖增錢數，以僥冒榮賞。

translations.literal: In recent years the monopoly goods office paid no heed to repeated certificate changes that harmed border planning, seeking only supplemental cash payment and specializing in buying southeastern salt certificates to inflate revenue and grasp honors by false pretense.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the monopoly goods office ignored how repeated certificate changes undermined frontier planning, demanding only supplemental cash and pushing southeastern salt certificates to inflate revenue and win promotion by fraud.

sentences.zh: 前鈔方行，而後鈔又復變易，特令先次支鹽，則前鈔遂為廢紙，罔人攘利，商旅怨嗟。

translations.literal: Earlier certificates had barely begun to circulate when later certificates changed again; by specially ordering salt paid out first, earlier certificates became waste paper; deceivers seized profit and merchants lamented.
translations.idiomatic: New certificates barely circulated before the rules changed again; prioritizing salt payouts left older certificates worthless, letting schemers profit while merchants groaned.

sentences.zh: 臣願明詔執政大臣，精擇能吏，推明鈔法，無以見行為有妨，無以既往為不可復，如薛向之法己效於昔者，可舉而行之。」

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that chief ministers be clearly instructed by edict to carefully select able officials, clarify the certificate law, not treat present practice as an obstacle, not treat what is past as irreparable — as with Xue Xiang's method that has already proven effective in former times, it may be raised up and enacted."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the chief ministers be plainly ordered to choose capable officials, restore the certificate system, neither treat current practice as an obstacle nor the past as beyond recovery — and enact proven methods such as Xue Xiang's."

sentences.zh: 今之練政事、通鈔法，不患無人；

translations.literal: Among those today skilled in administration who understand the certificate law, one need not worry that there are none;
translations.idiomatic: Capable administrators who understand certificate policy are not lacking today;

sentences.zh: 在京三庫之積，皆四方郡縣所入，不患無備。

translations.literal: The reserves in the capital's three treasuries all came from prefectures and counties everywhere; one need not worry about lack of preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's three treasuries were fed by counties across the realm, so reserves were not the problem.

sentences.zh: 如以三四百萬緡樁留京師，隨數以給鈔引，使鈔至給錢，不復邀阻，上下交信，則人以鈔引為輕齎，轉相貿易。

translations.literal: If three or four million strings were locked in reserve at the capital and certificates were paid out accordingly, so that upon arrival certificates received cash without further obstruction and upper and lower exchanged trust, then people would treat certificates as portable wealth and trade them among one another.
translations.idiomatic: If three or four million strings were set aside at the capital and certificates redeemed on arrival without delay, restoring mutual trust, merchants would treat certificates as portable capital and pass them from hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 或支請多，惟轉廊就給東南末鹽鈔或度牒之類，如東南末鹽鈔或度牒敕牒唯許以鈔引就給外，餘並令在京以見錢入易，樁留以為鈔引之資，亦計之得者。

translations.literal: If disbursement requests were many, only transfer-corridor southeastern powdered salt certificates or ordination certificates and the like would be issued; aside from southeastern powdered salt certificates or ordination and patent documents permitted to be redeemed only by certificate, the rest should all be exchanged for cash in the capital and locked in reserve as backing for certificates — this too would be a sound calculation.
translations.idiomatic: When payouts exceeded cash on hand, transfer-corridor southeastern powdered salt certificates or ordination slips could be issued; everything except items redeemable only by certificate should be bought with cash in the capital and held as certificate reserves — a workable plan.

sentences.zh: 若舊出文鈔，亦當體究立法，量為分數，支鹽償之。

translations.literal: As for old issued paper certificates, legislation should also be carefully investigated, apportioned by fixed fractions, and redeemed with salt disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: For older paper certificates already issued, new rules should set proportional salt redemption.

sentences.zh: 自昔立法之難，非特造始，修復既廢，亦為非易。

translations.literal: Since ancient times the difficulty of legislation lay not only in first creation; restoring what had already been abandoned was also not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Legislation has always been hard — not only to create, but to revive once abandoned.

sentences.zh: 欲興經久之利，則目前微害，宜亦可略，惟詳酌可否施行之。

translations.literal: If one wishes to establish lasting benefit, then present minor harm may also be overlooked; only carefully weigh whether it can be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: To secure lasting gain, minor present costs may be tolerated; the question is whether the policy can be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 未幾，張商英為相，乃議變通損益，復熙、豐之舊，令內府錢別樁一千五百萬緡，餘悉移用，以革錢、鈔、物三等偏重之弊。

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Shangying became chancellor and proposed adjustments for gain and loss, restoring the Xi-Feng old system; he ordered fifteen million strings from the inner treasury separately locked in reserve, with the rest all repurposed, to reform the imbalance among cash, certificates, and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Shangying became chief councillor and proposed restoring Xi-Feng practice: fifteen million strings from the inner treasury would be reserved, the rest redirected, correcting the skew among cash, certificates, and commodities.

sentences.zh: 陝西給鈔五百萬緡，江、淮發運司給見錢文據或截兌上供錢三百萬緡。

translations.literal: Shaanxi was allotted five million strings in certificates; the Jiang-Huai transport commission provided cash vouchers or diverted tribute funds of three million strings.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi received five million strings in certificates; the Jiang-Huai transport commission supplied cash vouchers or diverted three million strings of tribute funds.

sentences.zh: 以左司員外郎張察措置東南鹽事，提舉江西常平張根管幹運淮鹽於江西，罷提舉鹽香，諸路鹽事各歸提刑司。

translations.literal: Left Department outside director Zhang Cha was assigned to arrange southeastern salt affairs; Jiangxi Ever-Normal intendant Zhang Gen was put in charge of transporting Huai salt into Jiangxi; the salt-and-incense intendant office was abolished, and salt affairs in each circuit returned to the judicial commissioner offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cha, outside director of the Left Department, was charged with southeastern salt; Zhang Gen, Jiangxi Ever-Normal intendant, managed Huai salt shipments into Jiangxi; the salt-and-incense intendant was abolished and salt affairs reverted to circuit judicial commissioners.

sentences.zh: 議定五等舊鈔，商旅已換請新鈔及見錢鈔不對帶，聽先給東南末鹽諸路貨易。

translations.literal: Five grades of old certificates were defined; merchants who had already exchanged for new certificates and cash-only certificates without pairing were permitted first disbursement of southeastern powdered salt for trade in the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Five grades of old certificates were fixed; merchants who had swapped for new or cash-only certificates without pairing were allowed first claim on southeastern powdered salt for intercircuit trade.

sentences.zh: 仍下淮、浙鹽場，以鹽十分率之，樁留五分，以待支發官綱，備三路商旅轉廊算請，餘五分以待算請新鈔及見錢鈔與不帶舊鈔當先給者。

translations.literal: Orders were also sent to Huai and Zhe salt works: calculating salt by ten parts, five parts were locked in reserve to await official convoy disbursement and to supply three-circuit merchant transfer-corridor claims, and the remaining five parts awaited claims by new certificates, cash certificates, and unpaired old certificates due for priority payout.
translations.idiomatic: Huai and Zhe salt works were ordered to divide salt into tenths: half reserved for official convoys and three-circuit transfer claims, half for new certificates, cash certificates, and unpaired old certificates due priority.

sentences.zh: 於是推行舊法，以商旅五色舊鈔，若用換請新鈔對帶，方許支鹽，慮伺候歲月，欲給無由，乃立增納之法。

translations.literal: The old law was then enforced: merchants' five-color old certificates were permitted salt disbursement only if paired with newly exchanged certificates; fearing months of waiting with no means of payout, a supplemental payment law was established.
translations.idiomatic: The old rule was restored: merchants' five-color old certificates could claim salt only when paired with new ones; fearing long waits with no payout, a supplemental payment scheme was introduced.

sentences.zh: 貼三鈔許於榷貨務更貼見緡七分，貼四鈔更貼六分，貼五、當十鈔貼七分，河北見錢文據貼五分算請。

translations.literal: Grade-three supplementary certificates were permitted at the monopoly goods office to add seven-tenths more in cash; grade-four certificates six-tenths more; grade-five and ten-for-one certificates seven-tenths more; Hebei cash vouchers five-tenths more for claim calculation.
translations.idiomatic: At the monopoly goods office, grade-three certificates required seventy percent supplemental cash; grade-four, sixty percent; grade-five and ten-for-one, seventy percent; Hebei cash vouchers, fifty percent to qualify for claims.

sentences.zh: 有司議，三路鈔法如熙、豐舊法，全仰東南末鹽為本，若許將舊鈔貼納算請，正與推行三路熙、豐鈔法相戾；

translations.literal: Officials debated: the three-circuit certificate law under the Xi-Feng old system relied wholly on southeastern powdered salt as its foundation; if old certificates were permitted supplemental payment for claims, this directly contradicted restoring the three-circuit Xi-Feng certificate law;
translations.idiomatic: Officials argued that the Xi-Feng three-circuit certificate system rested entirely on southeastern powdered salt, so allowing old certificates to claim through supplemental payment directly undercut restoration of that system;

sentences.zh: 即不令貼納算還，又鈔無所歸。

translations.literal: Yet if supplemental payment redemption were not permitted, certificates again had nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Yet banning supplemental redemption left certificates with no outlet.

sentences.zh: 議將河北見錢文據減增納二分，餘各減二分，以告敕、度牒、香藥、雜物、東南鹽算請給償。

translations.literal: It was agreed to reduce supplemental payment on Hebei cash vouchers by two-tenths and each of the others by two-tenths, redeeming claims with patents, ordination certificates, aromatics, miscellaneous goods, and southeastern salt.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed to cut supplemental payments by twenty percent on Hebei cash vouchers and twenty percent on the rest, redeeming claims with patents, ordination slips, aromatics, goods, and southeastern salt.

sentences.zh: 帝詔：「東南六路元豐年額賣鹽錢，以緡計之，諸路各不下數十萬。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict: "The Yuanfeng annual salt-sale revenue quotas of the southeastern six circuits, calculated in strings, were in each circuit no less than several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered: "Under Yuanfeng each of the southeastern six circuits sold salt worth at least several hundred thousand strings annually.

sentences.zh: 自行鈔鹽，漕計窘匱，以江西言之，和、預買欠民價不少，何以副仁民愛物之意？」

translations.literal: Since the certificate-salt system, transport finances grew strained; taking Jiangxi as an example, cooperative and advance purchases owed the people no small amount in unpaid prices — how does this fulfill the intent of benevolence toward the people and care for their goods?"
translations.idiomatic: Since certificate salt, transport budgets have tightened; in Jiangxi alone cooperative and advance purchases owe substantial sums to the people — how does that honor humane governance?"

sentences.zh: 令東南諸路轉運司協力措置般運。

translations.literal: He ordered the transport commissions of the southeastern circuits to jointly arrange transport.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded southeastern transport commissions to coordinate shipments together.

sentences.zh: 政和元年，詔商旅願依熙、豐法轉廊者，許先次用三路新鈔算請，往他所定價給賣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenghe an edict stated that merchants wishing to use the transfer corridor under the Xi-Feng method were permitted first to claim with three-circuit new certificates and sell elsewhere at set prices.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 1 merchants who wished to trade via the Xi-Feng transfer corridor could claim salt first with new three-circuit certificates and sell it elsewhere at fixed prices.

sentences.zh: 優存兩浙亭戶額外中鹽，斤增價三分。

translations.literal: Two-Zhe saltern households' extra salt deliveries beyond quota were favorably preserved with a three-fen price increase per jin.
translations.idiomatic: Two-Zhe saltern households received favorable terms on extra salt deliveries, with prices raised three fen per jin.

sentences.zh: 已而張察均定鹽價，視紹聖斤增二錢，詔從其說，仍斤增一錢。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zhang Cha fixed salt prices, viewing the Shaosheng increase of two cash per jin; an edict followed his proposal but added only one cash per jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cha then set uniform salt prices, citing Shaosheng's two-cash-per-jin increase; the court accepted his plan but added only one cash per jin.

sentences.zh: 議者謂：「異時鹽商於榷貨務入納轉廊，惟視東南諸郡積鹽多寡，鹽多則請鈔者眾，所入亦倍，其闕鹽地，客不肯住。

translations.literal: Advisers said: "In former times when salt merchants paid in at the monopoly goods office for the transfer corridor, they looked only at how much salt the southeastern prefectures had stockpiled; where salt was abundant, certificate seekers were many and revenue doubled; where salt was lacking, merchants would not stay.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers noted: "Formerly salt merchants at the monopoly goods office watched southeastern stockpiles; abundant salt drew certificate seekers and doubled revenue, but merchants would not linger where salt ran short.

sentences.zh: 在元豐時遠地須預備二年或三年，次遠一年至二年，最近亦半年及一年，謂之準備鹽，而後鈔法乃通。

translations.literal: Under Yuanfeng distant regions had to prepare two or three years' salt, mid-distance regions one to two years, and nearest regions half a year to a full year — called prepared salt — and only then did the certificate law circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanfeng distant areas kept two or three years' prepared salt, mid-range areas one to two years, nearest areas six months to a year; only then did certificates circulate smoothly.

sentences.zh: 紹聖間遵用舊制，廣有準備，故均價之後，課利增倍。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng the old system was followed with ample preparation, so after price averaging revenue doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng restored the old system with ample reserves, and after prices were averaged revenue doubled.

sentences.zh: 謂宜嚴責轉運司般運準備鹽外，更及元豐準備之數，則鈔法始通，課利且羨。

translations.literal: They said transport commissions should be strictly charged, beyond transporting prepared salt, to reach Yuanfeng preparation levels; then the certificate law would circulate and revenue would moreover grow abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissions should be pressed not only to ship prepared salt but to match Yuanfeng reserve levels; then certificates would flow and revenue would swell.

sentences.zh: 亭戶煎鹽官為買納，比舊既增矣，止用元豐舊價自可，況用新價，而有本錢，復加借貸，何慮不增？

translations.literal: Saltern households boiled salt and the government bought it; prices had already risen above the old level; using only the Yuanfeng old price would suffice — moreover with new prices, capital funds, and added loans, why worry revenue would not increase?
translations.idiomatic: The state already bought saltern salt at prices above the old rate; Yuanfeng prices alone would suffice, and with new prices, capital advances, and loans, why doubt revenue would grow?

sentences.zh: 若斤更增一錢，虛費亦大。」

translations.literal: If one more cash were added per jin, wasteful expenditure would also be great."
translations.idiomatic: Adding another cash per jin would waste far too much."

sentences.zh: 詔施行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the policy enacted.

sentences.zh: 六路通置提舉鹽事官，置司於揚州，未幾罷。

translations.literal: The six circuits jointly established salt affairs intendant officials with an office at Yangzhou; before long it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The six circuits jointly appointed salt intendant officials based at Yangzhou, but the office was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 議者復謂：「客人在京榷貨務買東南末鹽者，其法有二：一曰見錢入納，二曰鈔麵轉廊。

translations.literal: Advisers again said: "Merchants buying southeastern powdered salt at the capital monopoly goods office had two methods: first, cash payment; second, certificate-face transfer corridor.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers added: "Merchants buying southeastern powdered salt at the capital monopoly goods office had two routes: pay in cash, or use the certificate-face transfer corridor.

sentences.zh: 今既許三路文鈔得以轉廊，若更循舊制，許以見錢入納，則客旅之錢，當入於榷貨，而不入於兼並，見錢留於京師，客旅走於東南。」

translations.literal: Now that three-circuit paper certificates are permitted for the transfer corridor, if the old system is further followed and cash payment is permitted, then merchants' money should enter the monopoly goods office and not enter private hoarding; cash would remain at the capital and merchants would travel to the southeast."
translations.idiomatic: With three-circuit paper certificates already allowed for transfer, restoring cash payment would channel merchant money into the monopoly goods office rather than private hoards — cash staying in the capital while merchants head southeast."

sentences.zh: 詔采用焉。

translations.literal: An edict adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又有謂：「舊法聽以物貨及官錢鈔引抵當，所以扶持鈔價，不大減損，昨禁之非是。

translations.literal: Another said: "The old law permitted goods and official cash certificates as collateral to uphold certificate value without great depreciation; yesterday's prohibition was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Others argued: "The old law allowed goods and official cash certificates as collateral to support certificate value; banning that was a mistake.

sentences.zh: 其舊轉廊鹽鈔，販至東南，轉運司乃專以見錢為務，致多壅閼。」

translations.literal: Old transfer-corridor salt certificates sold in the southeast, yet transport commissions made cash their sole concern, causing much blockage."
translations.idiomatic: Old transfer-corridor salt certificates reached the southeast, but transport offices insisted on cash alone, clogging the trade."

sentences.zh: 於是復鈔引抵當，一如其舊。

translations.literal: Certificate collateral was then restored exactly as before.
translations.idiomatic: Certificate collateral was restored as it had been.

sentences.zh: 末鹽以十分率之，限以八分給末鈔，二分許煮見緡，後又增見緡為三分。

translations.literal: Powdered salt was calculated by ten parts: eight parts limited to powdered-salt certificates, two parts permitted boiling payment in cash; later cash payment was increased to three parts.
translations.idiomatic: Powdered salt was divided into tenths: eight parts paid in powdered-salt certificates, two in cash for boiling; later the cash share rose to three tenths.

sentences.zh: 二年，江寧府、廣德軍、太平州斤更增錢二，宣、歙、饒、信州斤增錢三，池江州、南康軍斤增錢四，各以去產鹽地遠近為差。

translations.literal: In the second year Jiangning Prefecture, Guangde Army, and Taizhou added two cash per jin; Xuan, She, Rao, and Xin Prefectures added three cash per jin; Chizhou, Jiangzhou, and Nankang Army added four cash per jin — each according to distance from salt-producing regions.
translations.idiomatic: In year two Jiangning, Guangde, and Taizhou raised prices two cash per jin; Xuan, She, Rao, and Xin three cash; Chizhou, Jiangzhou, and Nankang four — graded by distance from production areas.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蔡京復用事，大變鹽法。

translations.literal: That year Cai Jing returned to power and greatly changed the salt law.
translations.idiomatic: That year Cai Jing regained influence and overhauled the salt system.

sentences.zh: 五月，罷官般賣，令商旅赴場請販，已般鹽並封樁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month official transport-and-sale was abolished; merchants were ordered to apply at salt works to purchase; already transported salt was all sealed in reserve.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the state stopped transporting and selling salt itself; merchants applied at the works to buy, and salt already in transit was sealed in store.

sentences.zh: 商旅赴榷貨務算請，先至者增支鹽以示勸。

translations.literal: Merchants claiming at the monopoly goods office received extra salt disbursement if they arrived first, as encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants filing claims at the monopoly goods office received bonus salt if they arrived first, as an incentive.

sentences.zh: 前轉廊已算鈔未支者，率百緡別輸見緡三分，仍用新鈔帶給舊鈔三分；

translations.literal: For prior transfer-corridor certificates already calculated but not yet disbursed, per one hundred strings an additional three-tenths in cash was paid separately, and new certificates still had to pair three-tenths of old certificates;
translations.idiomatic: For earlier transfer-corridor certificates calculated but unpaid, merchants paid thirty percent supplemental cash per hundred strings and paired new certificates with thirty percent of the old;

sentences.zh: 已算支者，所在抄數別輸帶賣如上法。

translations.literal: For those already calculated and disbursed, each locality copied the count and separately assessed paired sale as in the above method.
translations.idiomatic: Where claims had already been paid, each locality recorded the amounts and applied the same paired-sale rule.

sentences.zh: 其算請悉用見緡，而給鹽倫次，以全用見緡不帶舊鹽者為上，帶舊鹽者次之，帶舊鈔者又次之。

translations.literal: All claims used cash entirely, and the order of salt disbursement ranked first those paying wholly in cash without old salt, second those with old salt, and third those with old certificates.
translations.idiomatic: All claims were paid in cash; salt was issued in priority to full-cash buyers without old salt, then those with old salt, then those with old certificates.

sentences.zh: 三路糴買文鈔，算給七分東南末鹽者，聽對見緡支算二分，東北鹽亦如之。

translations.literal: Three-circuit procurement paper certificates redeemable for seven-tenths southeastern powdered salt were permitted to pair two-tenths cash for calculation; northeastern salt was treated likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Three-circuit procurement certificates redeemable seventy percent in southeastern powdered salt could pair twenty percent cash; northeastern salt followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 自餘文鈔，毋得一例對算。

translations.literal: All other paper certificates were not permitted uniform paired calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Other paper certificates could not all be paired under one rule.

sentences.zh: 復置諸路提舉官。

translations.literal: Circuit intendant officials were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendant posts were reinstated.

sentences.zh: 於是詔書褒美京功，然商旅終以法令不信為疑，算請者少，乃申扇搖之令，增賞錢五百緡。

translations.literal: An edict then praised Cai Jing's achievements, yet merchants still doubted because laws were untrustworthy; claimants were few, so the fan-shaking order was reissued with a bonus of five hundred strings.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Cai Jing's work, but merchants mistrusted the ever-changing rules and few filed claims; the fan-shaking incentive was revived with a five-hundred-string bonus.

sentences.zh: 三年，以商人承前先即諸州投勾，乃請鹽於場，留滯，罷之。

translations.literal: In the third year, because merchants preemptively filed at various prefectures before claiming salt at the works, causing delay, this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In year three merchants had been filing early at prefectures before claiming salt at the works, causing delays — the practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 若請鹽大帶斤重者，官為秤驗，乃輸錢給鈔。

translations.literal: If salt claimed in large bulk by jin weight, officials weighed and verified it before accepting payment and issuing certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Large bulk salt claims were officially weighed before payment and certificates were issued.

sentences.zh: 時法既屢變，蔡京更欲巧籠商賈之利，乃議措置十六條，裁定買官鹽價，囊以三百斤，價以十千，其鬻者聽增損隨時，舊加饒腳耗並罷。

translations.literal: Laws had already changed repeatedly; Cai Jing further wished to cleverly trap merchant profit and proposed sixteen provisions, fixing the price for buying official salt at bags of three hundred jin for ten thousand cash; sellers were permitted to adjust up or down with the times, and old surplus allowances for tare and loss were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: With laws shifting constantly, Cai Jing sought to capture merchant profits through sixteen new rules: official salt sold in three-hundred-jin bags for ten thousand cash, with prices adjustable over time and old surplus allowances abolished.

sentences.zh: 客鹽舊止船貯，改依東北鹽用囊，官袋鬻之，書印及私造貼補，並如茶籠篰法，仍禁再用。

translations.literal: Merchant salt formerly was stored only in boats; it was changed to follow northeastern salt in using bags, with official sacks sold; marking, printing, and private forgery or patching all followed the tea-crate law, and reuse was still forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant salt once stored aboard boats was bagged like northeastern salt in official sacks; marking and forgery rules followed the tea-crate system, and reuse was banned.

sentences.zh: 受鹽、支鹽官司，析而二之，受於場者管秤盤囊封，納於倉者管察視引據、合同號簿。

translations.literal: Receipt and disbursement offices for salt were split in two: those receiving at the works managed weighing, sealing bags; those receiving at warehouses inspected warrants, contracts, and ledger numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Salt receipt and disbursement were split: works officials weighed and sealed bags; warehouse officials checked warrants, contracts, and ledgers.

sentences.zh: 囊二十，則以一折驗合同遞牒給商人外，東南末鹽諸場，仍給鈔引號簿；

translations.literal: For every twenty bags one verification contract and transit document was given to the merchant; at southeastern powdered salt works certificate ledgers were also issued;
translations.idiomatic: Every twenty bags earned one verification contract for the merchant; southeastern powdered salt works also issued certificate ledgers;

sentences.zh: 有欲改指別場者，並批銷號簿及鈔引，仍用合同遞牒報所指處給隨鹽引；

translations.literal: If one wished to redirect to another works, ledger numbers and certificates were all cancelled and marked void; a contract transit document still reported to the designated site to issue the accompanying salt warrant;
translations.idiomatic: Merchants changing destination had ledgers and certificates cancelled and notified the new site by contract to issue the accompanying salt warrant;

sentences.zh: 即已支鹽，關所指處籍記。

translations.literal: Once salt was disbursed, the designated site was notified for registry.
translations.idiomatic: After salt was issued, the designated site recorded the transaction.

sentences.zh: 中路改指者仿此。

translations.literal: Mid-route redirection followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-route changes followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 其引繳納，限以一年，有故展毋得逾半年；

translations.literal: Surrender of warrants was limited to one year; extensions for cause were not to exceed half a year;
translations.idiomatic: Warrants had to be surrendered within one year; extensions for cause could not exceed six months;

sentences.zh: 限竟，鹽未全售者毀引，以見鹽籍於官，止聽鬻其處，毋得翻改。

translations.literal: When the deadline ended, if salt was not fully sold the warrant was destroyed, remaining salt registered with the state, and sale permitted only at that place with no rerouting.
translations.idiomatic: At deadline unsold salt required destroying the warrant; remaining stock was registered with the state and could be sold only locally, with no rerouting.

sentences.zh: 大抵皆視茶法而多為節目，欺奪民利，故以免究盜販、私煎、大帶斤重為名，而專用對帶之法。

translations.literal: For the most part all followed the tea law with many additional clauses, seizing the people's profit; under the pretext of exempting investigation of smuggling, private boiling, and large bulk by jin weight, they exclusively used the paired-certificate method.
translations.idiomatic: Most rules copied the tea monopoly with added clauses that seized merchant profit — nominally to stop smuggling, private boiling, and bulk claims, but in practice relying entirely on paired certificates.

sentences.zh: 客負鈔請鹽，往往厄不即畀，必對元數再買新鈔，方聽帶給舊鈔之半。

translations.literal: Merchants holding certificates to claim salt were often obstructed and not immediately given salt; they had to match the original amount and buy new certificates again before half payment on old certificates was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants with certificates were often denied immediate salt; they had to buy new certificates matching the original amount before receiving half on the old ones.

sentences.zh: 慮令之不行也，嚴避免之禁，申沮壞之制，重扇搖之法，季輒比較，務峻督責以取辦。

translations.literal: Fearing the orders would not be carried out, evasion was strictly forbidden, sabotage penalties were reissued, fan-shaking methods were weighted heavily, and quarterly comparisons were made, striving for harsh supervision and accountability to secure completion.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing noncompliance, the state tightened evasion bans, sabotage penalties, and fan-shaking rewards, comparing results each quarter and driving officials hard to deliver.

sentences.zh: 四年，以遠地商販者稀，鹽倉以地遠近為敘，先給遠者。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because distant regions had few merchants, salt depots ranked by distance and paid out to distant regions first.
translations.idiomatic: In year four distant regions drew few merchants, so salt depots prioritized distant areas in disbursement.

sentences.zh: 繼令搭帶正鹽，期一月不買新鈔，沒官，而剩鹽即沒納。

translations.literal: It was next ordered that bundled official salt required purchase of new certificates within one month or forfeiture to the state, and surplus salt was immediately confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants then had to buy new certificates within a month when bundled with official salt or forfeit to the state; surplus salt was confiscated on the spot.

sentences.zh: 五年，偽造引者並依川錢引定罪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, those who forged warrants were all punished according to the Sichuan money-warrant statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In year five forged warrants were punished under the Sichuan money-warrant laws.

sentences.zh: 六年，以產鹽州軍大商弗肯止留，其用小袋住賣者聽輸錢二十給鈔，毋得輒出州界。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because major merchants in salt-producing prefectures and armies would not stay, those who sold locally in small bags were permitted to pay twenty cash for certificates but were not permitted to leave the prefecture boundary.
translations.idiomatic: In year six major merchants refused to remain in producing regions; small-bag local sellers could pay twenty cash for a certificate but could not cross the prefecture border.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，詔六路封樁舊鹽數輸億萬，其聽商旅般販，與淮、浙鹽倉即今鹽鈔對算。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe an edict stated that old salt sealed in reserve in the six circuits numbered in the hundreds of millions; merchants were permitted to transport and sell it, pairing with Huai-Zhe salt depots against current salt certificates.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 2 the six circuits held hundreds of millions in sealed old salt; merchants could transport and sell it, pairing with Huai-Zhe depots against current salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 四年，榷貨務建議：「古有斗米斤鹽之說，熙、豐以前，米石不過六七百，時鹽價斤為錢六七十；

translations.literal: In the fourth year the monopoly goods office proposed: "Anciently there was the saying of one dou of rice to one jin of salt; before Xi-Feng a picul of rice was no more than six or seven hundred, and salt price per jin was sixty or seventy cash;
translations.idiomatic: In year four the monopoly goods office argued: "Tradition held one dou of rice to one jin of salt; before Xi-Feng rice cost six or seven hundred per picul and salt sixty or seventy cash per jin;

sentences.zh: 今米價石兩千五百至三千，而鹽仍舊六十。

translations.literal: Now rice price per picul is two thousand five hundred to three thousand, yet salt remains at sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Today rice runs twenty-five hundred to three thousand per picul while salt still sells for sixty.

sentences.zh: 崇寧會定鹽價，買鹽折算，酌以中價，斤為錢四十，今一斤三十七錢，虧公稍多。

translations.literal: Chongning fixed salt prices by converting purchase salt and taking the middle price at forty cash per jin; now one jin is thirty-seven cash — the state's loss is rather great.
translations.idiomatic: Chongning had set salt at forty cash per jin by averaging purchase prices; at thirty-seven cash per jin the state lost considerably.

sentences.zh: 欲囊增為十三千入納，而亭戶所輸並增價，庶克自贍，盜販衰止。」

translations.literal: They wished to raise bag intake price to thirteen thousand and also raise saltern household delivery prices, so that they might become self-supporting and smuggling would decline and cease."
translations.idiomatic: They proposed raising bag prices to thirteen thousand and saltern household payments accordingly, so households could support themselves and smuggling would fade."

sentences.zh: 於是舊鹽盡禁住賣，而籍記、貼輸、帶賣之令復用焉。

translations.literal: Old salt sales were entirely forbidden, and orders for registry, supplemental payment, and paired sale were again applied.
translations.idiomatic: Old salt sales were banned, and registration, supplemental payment, and paired-sale rules were restored.

sentences.zh: 初，鹽鈔法之行，積鹽於解池，積錢於京師榷貨務，積鈔於陝西沿邊諸郡。

translations.literal: Initially when the salt-certificate law was implemented, salt accumulated at Jie Lake, cash at the capital monopoly goods office, and certificates in Shaanxi's border prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the salt-certificate system began, salt pooled at Jie Lake, cash at the capital monopoly goods office, and certificates at Shaanxi's frontier counties.

sentences.zh: 商賈以物斛至邊入中，請鈔以歸。

translations.literal: Merchants brought grain measures to the border to deliver in and requested certificates to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants hauled grain to the frontier, delivered it in, and took certificates home.

sentences.zh: 物斛至邊有數倍之息，惟患無回貨，故極利於得鈔，徑請鹽於解池，而解鹽通行地甚寬；

translations.literal: Grain measures reaching the border yielded several-fold profit; the only worry was lack of return cargo, so obtaining certificates was extremely profitable — one could directly request salt at Jie Lake, and Jie salt's circulation area was very broad;
translations.idiomatic: Frontier grain brought several-fold profit, but merchants lacked return cargo — certificates solved that; they could claim Jie salt directly, and Jie salt sold across a wide market;

sentences.zh: 或請錢於京師，每鈔六千二百，登時給與，但輸頭子等錢數十而已。

translations.literal: Or one could request cash at the capital — six thousand two hundred per certificate, paid on the spot, requiring only payment of several tens in copper cash fees.
translations.idiomatic: Or they could redeem cash at the capital — six thousand two hundred per certificate, paid instantly, for a fee of only a few dozen copper cash.

sentences.zh: 以此所由州縣，貿易者甚眾。

translations.literal: Because of this the prefectures and counties along the routes had very many traders.
translations.idiomatic: Trade flourished in every county along the routes.

sentences.zh: 崇寧間，蔡京始變法，俾商人先輸錢請鈔，赴產鹽郡授鹽，欲囊括四方之錢，盡入中都，以進羨要寵，鈔法遂廢，商賈不通，邊儲失備；

translations.literal: During Chongning Cai Jing first changed the law, making merchants pay cash first to request certificates and go to salt-producing prefectures to receive salt, wishing to gather all money from the four directions into the central capital to advance surplus revenue and seek favor; the certificate law was then abandoned, merchants no longer circulated, and border stores lost preparedness;
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongning Cai Jing changed the rules: merchants paid first for certificates and collected salt at the source, aiming to drain money from every region into the capital and win favor with inflated revenue; the certificate system collapsed, trade stalled, and frontier reserves emptied;

sentences.zh: 東南鹽禁加密，犯法被罪者多。

translations.literal: Southeastern salt prohibitions grew tighter, and many who violated the law were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Southeastern salt controls tightened, and prosecutions multiplied.

sentences.zh: 民間食鹽，雜以灰土。

translations.literal: Among the people, salt for eating was mixed with ash and soil.
translations.idiomatic: The salt people ate was adulterated with ash and dirt.

sentences.zh: 解池天產美利，乃與糞壤俱積矣。

translations.literal: Jie Lake's heaven-produced fine profit was thus accumulated together with dung soil.
translations.idiomatic: The fine salt heaven produced at Jie Lake piled up instead alongside muck and refuse.

sentences.zh: 大概常使見行之法售給才通，輒復變易，名對帶法。

translations.literal: In general they constantly made the currently applied method barely sufficient for sale and delivery, then again changed it; it was called the paired-certificate method.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule they let the current system barely keep flowing, then changed it again—the so-called paired-certificate method.

sentences.zh: 季年又變對帶為循環。

translations.literal: In the final year they again changed paired-certificate into circulation.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the year paired certificates had become the circulation system.

sentences.zh: 循環者，已賣鈔，未授鹽，復更鈔；

translations.literal: Circulation means: having already sold certificates, salt not yet delivered, again exchanging certificates;
translations.idiomatic: Under circulation, once certificates were sold but salt not yet issued, merchants had to exchange them again;

sentences.zh: 已更鈔，鹽未給，復貼輸錢，凡三輸錢，始獲一直之貨。

translations.literal: Having exchanged certificates, salt not yet supplied, again paying supplemental delivery money; in all three payments of money before obtaining one straight value in goods.
translations.idiomatic: After reissuing certificates, if salt still was not delivered, a supplemental payment was demanded—three separate payments in all before one honest load of salt was obtained.

sentences.zh: 民無貲更鈔，已輸錢悉乾沒，數十萬券一夕廢棄，朝為豪商，夕儕流丐，有赴水投繯而死者。

translations.literal: The people had no capital to exchange certificates; money already paid was all confiscated outright; hundreds of thousands of vouchers were abandoned overnight. Morning wealthy merchants, evening ranked with wandering beggars; some threw themselves into water or hanged themselves and died.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could not afford to exchange certificates lost every coin they had paid; hundreds of thousands of vouchers were voided overnight. Men who were great merchants at dawn were beggars by dusk; some drowned themselves or hanged themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 時有魏伯芻者，本省大胥，蔡京委信之，專主榷貨務。

translations.literal: At that time there was one Wei Bochu, a senior clerk of the province, whom Cai Jing entrusted and relied upon, exclusively in charge of the monopoly goods office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a senior provincial clerk named Wei Bochu enjoyed Cai Jing's full trust and ran the monopoly goods office.

sentences.zh: 政和六年，鹽課通及四千萬緡，官吏皆進秩。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe, salt revenue in total reached forty million strings; officials all received rank advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenghe, salt revenue passed forty million strings, and every official involved was promoted.

sentences.zh: 七年，又以課羨第賞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, again by surplus revenue ranking they were rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The next year rewards were apportioned by how much revenue exceeded quota.

sentences.zh: 伯芻年除歲遷，積官通議大夫、徽猷閣待制，既而黨附王黼，京惡而黜之。

translations.literal: Bochu year upon year dismissed and year upon year transferred; accumulated office to Righteousness Discussion Grandee, Awaiting Orders at the Splendid Writings Pavilion; thereafter factionally attached to Wang Fu, and Jing loathed and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Bochu was promoted every year until he held the ranks of Grand Master for Discussion of Governance and Awaiting Orders at the Splendid Writings Pavilion; he then sided with Wang Fu, and Cai Jing had him removed.

sentences.zh: 伯芻非有心計，但與交引戶關通，凡商旅算請，率克留十分之四以充入納之數，務入納數多，以昧人主而張虛最。

translations.literal: Bochu was not skilled in calculation, but colluded with exchange-certificate households; for every merchant's application he routinely withheld four-tenths to fill intake numbers, striving for high intake figures to deceive the ruler and inflate false records of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Bochu was no accountant, but he colluded with certificate brokers and routinely skimmed forty percent of every merchant application to pad intake totals, deceiving the throne with inflated performance figures.

sentences.zh: 初，政和再更鹽法，伯芻方為蔡京所倚信，建言：「朝廷所以開闔利柄，馳走商賈，不煩號令，億萬之錢輻湊而至。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zhenghe again changed the salt law, Bochu was just then relied upon and trusted by Cai Jing; he submitted advice: "The court thereby opens and closes the lever of profit, drives merchants to run about, without troubling with orders, and hundreds of millions in cash converges and arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenghe revised the salt law again, Bochu was in Cai Jing's confidence and memorialized: "The court need only open and close the profit lever to set merchants running—no orders required—and millions upon millions pour in.

sentences.zh: 禦府頒索，百司支費，歲用之外沛然有餘，則榷鹽之入可謂厚矣。

translations.literal: The imperial treasury distributes and demands; the hundred offices pay expenses; beyond annual use there is abundantly surplus—then salt monopoly revenue may be called substantial.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial treasury draws freely, ministries spend freely, and surplus remains after the year's needs—salt monopoly income has become truly vast.

sentences.zh: 頃年，鹽法未有一定之制，隨時變革以便公私，防閑未定，奸弊百出。

translations.literal: In recent years the salt law had no fixed system; it was changed from time to time for public and private convenience; safeguards were unsettled, and fraud and abuse emerged everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the salt law had no fixed form, shifting whenever it suited officials or merchants; with no stable controls, abuse flourished on every side.

sentences.zh: 自政和立法之後，頓絕弊源，公私兼利。

translations.literal: Since Zhenghe established the law, the sources of abuse were abruptly cut off; public and private both profited.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhenghe codified the law, the worst abuses had ceased and both state and people benefited.

sentences.zh: 異時一日所收不過二萬緡，則已詫其太多，今日之納乃常及四五萬貫。

translations.literal: Formerly a day's intake did not exceed twenty thousand strings, and that was already marveled at as too much; today's intake routinely reaches forty or fifty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Once a daily intake of twenty thousand strings was thought enormous; now forty or fifty thousand is routine.

sentences.zh: 以歲計之，有一郡而客鈔錢及五十餘萬貫者，處州是也；

translations.literal: Calculated by the year, there was one prefecture whose merchant certificate money reached more than five hundred thousand strings—Chuzhou was such a case;
translations.idiomatic: On an annual basis, one prefecture—Chuzhou—collected more than five hundred thousand strings in certificate money;

sentences.zh: 有一州倉而客人請鹽及四十萬袋者，泰州是也。

translations.literal: There was one prefectural warehouse at which merchants requested salt reaching four hundred thousand bags—Taizhou was such a case.
translations.idiomatic: and one prefectural warehouse—Taizhou's—where merchants drew more than four hundred thousand bags of salt.

sentences.zh: 新法於今才二年，而所收已及四千萬貫，雖傳記所載貫朽錢流者，實未足為今日道也。

translations.literal: The new law has been in force only two years to now, yet intake already reached forty million strings; although histories record strings rotting and cash flowing, that truly is not enough to describe today.
translations.idiomatic: The new law was barely two years old and had already taken in forty million strings—more than the old saying about money rotting from abundance could express.

sentences.zh: 伏乞以通收四千萬貫之數，宣付史館，以示富國裕民之政。」

translations.literal: I humbly request that the total intake figure of forty million strings be proclaimed and delivered to the historiography office, to show the policy of enriching the state and benefiting the people."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that this forty-million-string total be recorded at the historiography office as proof of a policy that enriches the state and the people."

sentences.zh: 小人得時騁誌，無所顧忌，遂至於此。

translations.literal: Petty men, gaining the times, gave free rein to their ambitions without any scruple, and so it reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the end when petty men, emboldened by the moment, pursued their ambitions without restraint.

sentences.zh: 於時禦府用度日廣，課入欲豐，再申歲較季比之令，在職而暫取告，其月日皆毋得計折，害法者不以官蔭並處極坐，微至於鹽袋鯗鹽，莫不有禁，州縣惟務歲增課以避罪法，上下程督加厲。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial treasury's daily use grew ever wider; revenue intake was desired to be abundant; again the order for annual comparison and quarterly ranking was proclaimed. Those on duty who temporarily took leave—their month and day counts were all not permitted to be credited; those harming the law were not spared by official privilege from the severest punishment. Even down to salt bags and cured salt, nothing lacked prohibition. Prefectures and counties only strove to increase revenue year by year to avoid penal law; superiors and subordinates pressed and supervised with added severity.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial spending kept rising and revenue targets grew ever higher; annual comparisons and quarterly rankings were reimposed. Leave days no longer counted toward quotas, and even official privilege could not shield violators from the harshest penalties. Rules reached down to individual salt bags and cured salt. Counties raced to raise quotas and avoid punishment while superiors pressed them ever harder.

sentences.zh: 七年，乃詔：「昨改鹽法，立賞至重，抑配者多，計口敷及嬰孩，廣數下逮駝畜，使良民受弊，比屋愁歎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict was issued: "Yesterday's revision of the salt law established rewards of extreme weight; forced allocations were many; counting mouths reached even infants; broad reckoning extended down to camels and livestock, causing good commoners to suffer harm; house after house groaned in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict declared: "The recent salt-law changes set heavy rewards and forced allocations so widely that even infants and pack animals were counted, good households suffered, and every home groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 悉從初令，以利百姓。

translations.literal: All follow the original orders, to benefit the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Everything shall revert to the original orders for the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 三省其申嚴近製，改奉新鈔。」

translations.literal: The Three Departments should strictly proclaim recent regulations and change to observe new certificates."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments were to enforce the recent rules and adopt the new certificates."

sentences.zh: 然有司不能承守，故比較已罷而復用，抄劄既免而復行，鹽囊既增而復止，一囊之價裁為十一千，既又復為十三千，民力因以擾匱，而盜賊滋焉。

translations.literal: Yet the responsible offices could not uphold and preserve them. Thus comparisons already abolished were again applied; surcharges already exempted were again enforced; bag prices already raised were again halted. One bag's price was cut to eleven thousand, then again restored to thirteen thousand. The people's strength was thereby disturbed and exhausted, and bandits and robbers multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials failed to comply. Abolished comparisons were restored, waived surcharges reimposed, and bag prices yo-yoed between eleven and thirteen thousand. The people were worn down and banditry spread.

sentences.zh: 南渡，淮、浙亭戶，官給本錢。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, Huai and Zhe saltern households received capital advances from the government.
translations.idiomatic: After the court fled south, saltern households in Huai and Zhe received capital advances from the state.

sentences.zh: 諸州置倉，令商人買鈔，五十斤為石，六石為袋，輸鈔錢十八千。

translations.literal: Prefectures established warehouses and ordered merchants to buy certificates: fifty jin made one picul, six piculs one bag; certificate money paid was eighteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures set up warehouses and sold certificates to merchants at eighteen thousand per bag—fifty jin to the picul, six piculs to the bag.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，詔臨安府，秀州亭戶二稅，依皇祐法輸鹽，立監官不察亭戶私煎及巡捕漏泄之法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, an edict to Lin'an Prefecture: Xiuzhou saltern households' two taxes, following the Huangyou law deliver salt; establish supervising officials and laws against failing to inspect saltern households' private boiling and against patrol capture leaks.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing's first year an edict ordered Lin'an and Xiuzhou saltern households to pay their two taxes in salt under the Huangyou rules, with supervising officials and patrol laws against private boiling and leaks.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，詔淮、浙鹽令商人袋貼輸通貨錢三千，已算請而未售者亦如之，十日不自陳，如私鹽律。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year, an edict on Huai and Zhe salt ordered merchants to pay three thousand in circulating currency per bag as supplemental delivery; those already calculated and requested but not yet sold were likewise treated; if within ten days they did not self-report, they were treated under illicit-salt law.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year merchants in Huai and Zhe were ordered to pay three thousand in currency per bag as a supplemental fee; holders of certificates already issued but unsold faced the same rule, and failure to report within ten days brought illicit-salt penalties.

sentences.zh: 時呂頤浩用提轄張純儀，峻更鹽法。

translations.literal: At the time Lü Yihao employed Supervising Commissioner Zhang Chunyi and severely changed the salt law.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yihao then relied on Supervising Commissioner Zhang Chunyi to overhaul the salt law harshly.

sentences.zh: 十有一月，詔淮、浙鹽以十分為率，四分支今降旨符以後文鈔，四分支建炎渡江以後文鈔。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict on Huai and Zhe salt took ten parts as the rate: four parts disbursed with text certificates after the present descending edict, four parts disbursed with text certificates after the Jianyan river-crossing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Huai and Zhe salt was divided into tenths: four parts paid in certificates issued after the current edict, four parts in certificates issued after the Jianyan crossing.

sentences.zh: 先是呂頤浩以對帶法不可用，令商人貼輸錢，至是復以分數如對帶法，於是始加嚴酷矣。

translations.literal: Earlier Lü Yihao, because the paired-certificate method was unusable, ordered merchants to pay supplemental delivery money; reaching this point he again used fractional division like the paired-certificate method—thence strict severity began.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yihao had abandoned the paired-certificate method and required supplemental payments; now fractional redemption like paired certificates was restored—and the regime turned harsher.

sentences.zh: 三年，減民間蠶鹽錢。

translations.literal: In the third year, private silkworm-salt money was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the levy on private silkworm salt was cut.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，詔淮、浙鹽鈔錢每袋增貼輸錢三貫，並計綱輸行在，尋命廣鹽亦如之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, an edict on Huai and Zhe salt certificate money added three strings supplemental delivery money per bag, all calculated by transport convoy and delivered to the temporary capital; soon Guang salt was likewise ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Huai and Zhe certificate fees rose by three strings per bag, payable by convoy to the temporary capital; Guang salt soon followed.

sentences.zh: 九月，以入輸遲細，減所添錢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because intake delivery was slow and slight, the added money was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the supplemental fee was reduced because payments were coming in too slowly.

sentences.zh: 然自建炎三年改鈔法，及今所改，凡五變，而建炎舊鈔支尚未絕，乃命以先後並支焉。

translations.literal: Yet from the Jianyan third-year change of the certificate law to the present changes, in all there were five transformations; yet Jianyan old certificate disbursement had not yet ended—thereupon it was ordered that earlier and later be disbursed together.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jianyan third-year certificate reform to the present there had been five changes, yet old Jianyan certificates were still unredeemed—so all were ordered paid in sequence regardless of issue date.

sentences.zh: 孝宗乾道六年，戶部侍郎葉衡奏：「今日財賦，鬻海之利居其半，年來課入不增，商賈不行，皆私販害之也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiandao under Emperor Xiaozong, Vice Minister of Revenue Ye Heng memorialized: "Today's fiscal levies—sea salt monopoly profit occupies half; in recent years revenue intake has not increased and merchants do not operate—all are harmed by private trafficking.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qiandao, Vice Minister of Revenue Ye Heng reported: "Salt monopoly profits now make up half the state's revenue, yet intake has stagnated and legitimate trade has stalled—all because of smuggling.

sentences.zh: 且以淮東、二浙鹽出入之數言之，淮東鹽灶四百一十二所，歲額鹽二百六十八萬三千餘石，去年兩務場賣淮鹽六十七萬二千三百餘袋，收錢二千一百九十六萬三千餘貫；

translations.literal: Moreover, speaking of Huai-East and Two Zhe salt inflow and outflow figures: Huai-East salt ovens four hundred twelve sites; annual quota salt two million six hundred eighty-three thousand plus piculs; last year the two monopoly offices sold Huai salt six hundred seventy-two thousand three hundred plus bags, collecting cash twenty-one million nine hundred sixty-three thousand plus strings;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Huai-East and the Two Zhe circuits: Huai-East had 412 salt ovens and an annual quota of more than 2,683,000 piculs; last year its two monopoly offices sold more than 672,300 bags of Huai salt for more than 21,963,000 strings;

sentences.zh: 二浙課額一百九十七萬餘石，去年兩務場賣浙鹽二十萬二千餘袋，收錢五百一萬二千餘貫，而鹽灶乃計二千四百餘所。

translations.literal: Two Zhe quota one million nine hundred seventy thousand plus piculs; last year the two monopoly offices sold Zhe salt two hundred two thousand plus bags, collecting cash five million one hundred twenty thousand plus strings; yet salt ovens totaled two thousand four hundred plus sites.
translations.idiomatic: the Two Zhe quota exceeded 1,970,000 piculs, yet last year only 202,000 bags sold for just over 5,012,000 strings—despite more than 2,400 salt ovens.

sentences.zh: 以鹽額論之，淮東之數多於二浙五之一，以去歲賣鹽錢數論之，淮東多於二浙三之二，及以灶之多寡論之，兩浙反多淮東四之三，蓋二浙無非私販故也。

translations.literal: Judging by salt quota, Huai-East's figure exceeds Two Zhe by one-fifth; judging by last year's salt-sale cash figures, Huai-East exceeds Two Zhe by two-thirds; and judging by the many or few of ovens, Two Zhe instead exceeds Huai-East by three-fourths—because Two Zhe is nothing but private trafficking.
translations.idiomatic: By quota Huai-East exceeded Two Zhe by a fifth; by last year's sales Huai-East took in two-thirds more cash; yet Two Zhe had three-quarters more ovens—clear proof that smuggling, not production, was the difference.

sentences.zh: 欲望遣官分路措置。」

translations.literal: I desire that officials be dispatched to arrange matters route by route."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that commissioners be sent to each route to address this."

sentences.zh: 淳熙八年，詔住賣帶賣積鹽，以朝廷徒有帶賣之名，總所未免有借撥之弊故也。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chunxi, an edict halted paired sale of accumulated salt, because the court had only the name of paired sale while the general office could not avoid the abuse of borrowing and reallocating.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chunxi paired sale of stockpiled salt was banned because the paired-sale label had masked borrowing and reallocation at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 十年，先是湖北鹽商吳傳言：「國家鬻海之利，以三分為率，淮東居其二。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, earlier Hubei salt merchant Wu Chuan said: "The state's sea-salt monopoly profit, taking three parts as the rate—Huai-East occupies two of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Hubei salt merchant Wu Chuan had argued: "Of the state's salt monopoly revenue, reckoned in thirds, Huai-East accounts for two.

sentences.zh: 通、泰、楚隸買鹽場十六，催煎場十二，灶四百十二。

translations.literal: Tong, Tai, and Chu had sixteen subordinate purchase-salt fields, twelve urging-boil fields, and four hundred twelve ovens.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, Tai, and Chu had sixteen purchase stations, twelve boiling stations, and 412 ovens.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，灶煎鹽多止十一籌，籌為鹽一百斤。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing, oven-boiled salt mostly stopped at eleven ladles; one ladle was one hundred jin of salt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaoxing most ovens produced no more than eleven ladles of salt, each ladle being one hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 淳熙初，亭戶得嘗試鹵水之法，灶煎至二十五籌至三十籌，增舊額之半。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunxi, saltern households obtained the method of testing brine; ovens boiled to twenty-five to thirty ladles, increasing the old quota by half.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunxi saltern households learned to test brine, raising output to twenty-five or thirty ladles per boil—half again the old quota.

sentences.zh: 緣此，鹽場買亭戶鹽，籌增稱鹽二十斤至三十斤為浮鹽。

translations.literal: Because of this, salt fields buying saltern household salt counted each ladle's added twenty to thirty jin of salt as floating/extra salt.
translations.idiomatic: Salt fields therefore counted an extra twenty to thirty jin per ladle as floating/extra salt when buying from saltern households.

sentences.zh: 日買鹽一萬餘籌，其浮鹽止以二十斤為則，有二十萬斤，為二千籌，籌為錢一貫八百三十文，內除船腳錢二百文，有一貫六百三十文。

translations.literal: Daily salt purchased exceeded ten thousand ladles; its floating/extra salt used only twenty jin as the standard—there were two hundred thousand jin, making two thousand ladles; one ladle was cash one string eight hundred thirty cash; deducting within ship freight money two hundred cash, there was one string six hundred thirty cash.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand ladles were bought daily; counting only twenty jin per ladle as floating/extra salt yielded two hundred thousand jin—two thousand ladles—at 1,830 cash per ladle, or 1,630 after deducting 200 cash for shipping.

sentences.zh: 其鹽並再中入官，為鈔錢四百五十一萬七千五百餘緡。

translations.literal: That salt, all counted again and entered into government accounts, amounted to certificate money four million five hundred seventeen thousand five hundred plus strings.
translations.idiomatic: Entering that salt twice into government accounts yielded more than 4,517,500 strings in certificate revenue.

sentences.zh: 又綱取鹽一代並諸窠名等，及賣又多稱斤兩，亭戶饑寒，不免私賣。

translations.literal: Moreover, convoys took one generation of salt quota and various nominal categories, and at sale they again overstated jin and ounces; saltern households, hungry and cold, could not avoid private sale.
translations.idiomatic: Convoys also seized a full generation's quota plus assorted fees, and sales were again overstated by weight—so hungry, cold saltern households had no choice but to sell privately.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷嚴究，還其本錢，而後可以盡革私賣之弊。」

translations.literal: If the court strictly investigated and returned their capital advances, then afterward private-sale abuses could be entirely reformed."
translations.idiomatic: If the court investigated strictly and repaid their capital, private sale could be fully suppressed."

sentences.zh: 至是，詔還通、泰等州諸鹽場欠亭戶鹽本錢一百一十萬貫。

translations.literal: Reaching this point, an edict returned to saltern households at Tong, Tai, and other prefectures' various salt fields owed salt capital advances of one million one hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then repaid 1,100,000 strings in capital owed to saltern households at salt fields in Tong, Tai, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 寧宗慶元初，詔罷循環鹽鈔，改增剩鈔名為正支文鈔給算，與已投倉者通理先後支散。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingyuan under Emperor Ningzong, an edict abolished circulation salt certificates, changed and renamed surplus certificates as regular-disbursement text certificates for calculation and payment, and jointly reckoned with those already submitted to warehouses earlier and later disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingyuan Emperor Ningzong abolished circulation salt certificates, renamed surplus certificates as regular-disbursement certificates, and ordered them paid together with certificates already lodged at warehouses, in sequence.

sentences.zh: 以淮東提舉陳損之言循環鈔多弊，故有是命。

translations.literal: Because Huai-East Intendant Chen Sun said circulation certificates had many abuses, therefore there was this order.
translations.idiomatic: The order followed Huai-East Intendant Chen Sun's report that circulation certificates bred endless abuse.

sentences.zh: 於是富商巨賈有願為貧民者矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon wealthy merchants and great traders had some who wished to become poor commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy merchants now wished they were poor men.

sentences.zh: 開禧二年，詔自今新鈔一袋，搭支舊鈔一袋；

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaixi, an edict: from now one new certificate bag paired with disbursement of one old certificate bag;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaixi an edict ordered that each new certificate bag be paired with one old certificate bag for redemption;

sentences.zh: 如新鈔多於舊鈔，或願全以新鈔支鹽，及無舊鈔而願全買新鈔者聽，以新鈔理資次。

translations.literal: If new certificates exceeded old certificates, or one wished entirely to disburse salt with new certificates, or having no old certificates yet wished entirely to buy new certificates—permitted; new certificates were used to arrange order of payment.
translations.idiomatic: if new certificates outnumbered old ones, holders might redeem entirely in new certificates or buy new certificates without old ones, ranked by date of new certificate purchase.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年，詔淮東貼輸鹽錢免二分交子，止用錢會中半。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiading, an edict on Huai-East supplemental salt money exempted two-tenths in exchange notes; only cash notes were used for half payment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiading Huai-East supplemental salt fees were exempted from two-tenths in paper exchange notes; only half could be paid in cash notes.

sentences.zh: 三年詔：「停鈔引之家，增長舊鈔價直，袋賣官會百貫以上。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict: "Households whose certificate circulation had halted—increase old certificate value; bags sold at official notes one hundred strings and above.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict declared: "For households whose certificates had ceased to circulate, raise the value of old certificates; bags shall sell for one hundred official notes or more.

sentences.zh: 自今令到日，鹽鈔官錢袋增收會子二十貫，三務場朱印於鈔麵，作「某年某月新鈔」，俟通賣及一百萬袋，即免增收。

translations.literal: From the day this order arrives, salt certificate official money per bag additionally collects twenty strings in notes; the three monopoly offices red-seal on the certificate face, making "such year such month new certificate"; when total sales reach one million bags, the additional collection is then exempted.
translations.idiomatic: From the order's effective date each salt certificate bag would carry an additional twenty strings in notes; the three monopoly offices would red-stamp certificates "new certificate, month and year," and the surcharge would end once one million bags had sold.

sentences.zh: 其日前已未支鹽鈔並為舊鈔，期以一年持赴倉場支鹽，袋貼輸官會一十貫，出限更不行用。」

translations.literal: Those certificates before that day already issued but salt not yet disbursed were all treated as old certificates; a deadline of one year to carry them to warehouse fields for salt disbursement; per bag supplemental delivery of ten strings in official notes; beyond the deadline they were no longer valid for use."
