translations.idiomatic: Certificates issued before that date but not yet redeemed were treated as old certificates, redeemable within one year at warehouses for ten official notes per bag; after the deadline they would be void."

sentences.zh: 此淮、浙鹽之大略也。

translations.literal: This is the general outline of Huai and Zhe salt.
translations.idiomatic: Such, in broad outline, was Huai and Zhe salt policy.

sentences.zh: 唐乾元初，第五琦為鹽鐵使，變鹽法，劉晏代之；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan in Tang, Diwu Qi was salt-and-iron commissioner and changed the salt law; Liu Yan replaced him;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tang Qianyuan, Diwu Qi reformed the salt law as salt-and-iron commissioner; Liu Yan succeeded him;

sentences.zh: 當時舉天下鹽利，歲才四十萬緡。

translations.literal: At that time the salt profit of the entire realm per year was only four hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time all salt profits under heaven came to only four hundred thousand strings a year.

sentences.zh: 至大曆，增至六百餘萬緡。

translations.literal: Reaching Dali, it increased to more than six million strings.
translations.idiomatic: By the Dali era it had risen to more than six million strings.

sentences.zh: 天下之賦，鹽利居半。

translations.literal: Of the realm's levies, salt profit occupied half.
translations.idiomatic: Salt profits made up half of all state revenue.

sentences.zh: 元祐間，淮鹽與解池等歲四百萬緡。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou, Huai salt together with Jie Lake and the like per year was four million strings.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou Huai salt and Jie Lake salt together yielded four million strings a year.

sentences.zh: 比唐舉天下之賦已三分之二。

translations.literal: Compared with Tang's levies for the entire realm, this was already two-thirds.
translations.idiomatic: That alone was two-thirds of all Tang revenue under heaven.

sentences.zh: 紹興末年以來，泰州海陵一監，支監三十餘萬席，為錢六七百萬緡，則是一州之數，過唐舉天下之數矣。

translations.literal: From the late Shaoxing years onward, one supervisor at Taizhou Hailing disbursed more than three hundred thousand seats, amounting to cash of six or seven million strings—then one prefecture's figure exceeded Tang's figure for the entire realm.
translations.idiomatic: Since late Shaoxing a single Taizhou Hailing supervisor alone disbursed more than three hundred thousand seats—six or seven million strings—so one prefecture now surpassed all Tang revenue under heaven.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年，監察御史趙至道言：「夫產鹽固藉於鹽戶，鬻鹽實賴於鹽商，故鹽戶所當存恤，鹽商所當優潤。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoqing, Investigating Censor Zhao Zhidao said: "Producing salt indeed relies on salt households; selling salt truly depends on salt merchants—therefore salt households ought to be preserved and cherished, salt merchants ought to be favored and enriched.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoqing Investigating Censor Zhao Zhidao argued: "Salt production depends on saltern households and salt sales on merchants—both must be protected and both must prosper.

sentences.zh: 慶元之初，歲為錢九百九十萬八千有奇，寶慶元年，止七百四十九萬九千有奇，乃知鹽課之虧，實鹽商之無所贏利。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingyuan, the year yielded cash nine million nine hundred eight thousand odd; in the first year of Baoqing, only seven million four hundred ninety-nine thousand odd—thus one knows the salt revenue deficit truly came from salt merchants having no profit.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qingyuan brought in 9,908,000 odd strings; Baoqing's first year only 7,499,000 odd—the deficit showed merchants could no longer turn a profit.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，莫若寬商旅，減征稅，庶幾慶元鹽課之盛，復見於今日矣。」

translations.literal: For today's plan, nothing is better than easing travel merchants, reducing levies and taxes—then perhaps Qingyuan salt revenue's flourishing may again appear in the present day."
translations.idiomatic: The remedy is to lighten burdens on traveling merchants and cut taxes, so Qingyuan's salt revenues might return."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，以侍御史李知孝言，罷上虞、餘姚海塗地創立鹽灶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding, on Attending Censor Li Zhixiao's advice, salt ovens newly established on tidal flats at Shangyu and Yuyao were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoding's first year, on Attending Censor Li Zhixiao's recommendation, salt ovens newly built on the tidal flats at Shangyu and Yuyao were shut down.

sentences.zh: 端平二年，都省言：「淮、浙歲額鹽九十七萬四千餘袋，近二三年積虧一百餘萬袋，民食貴鹽，公私俱病。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Duanping, the Imperial Secretariat said: "Huai and Zhe annual quota salt nine hundred seventy-four thousand plus bags; in the recent two or three years accumulated shortfall exceeds one million bags; the people eat dear salt; public and private both suffer."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duanping the Imperial Secretariat reported: "Huai and Zhe owe a quota of more than 974,000 bags, yet the last two or three years have fallen short by more than a million bags; people pay dear prices for salt and both state and subjects suffer."

sentences.zh: 有旨，三路提舉茶鹽司各置主管文字一員，專以興復鹽額、收買散鹽為務，歲終尚書省課其殿最。

translations.literal: An imperial directive: each of the three routes' tea-and-salt intendancies was to establish one clerk in charge of documents, exclusively tasked with restoring salt quotas and purchasing loose salt; at year's end the Ministry of Revenue assessed their grades of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered each of the three routes' tea-and-salt offices to appoint a clerk devoted to restoring quotas and buying up loose salt, with the Ministry of Revenue ranking their performance at year's end.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年，臣僚奏：「南渡立國，專仰鹽鈔，紹興、淳熙，率享其利。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou, officials memorialized: "After the southward crossing the state was established, relying exclusively on salt certificates; Shaoxing and Chunxi mostly enjoyed their profit.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou's first year officials memorialized: "Since the founding of the southern dynasty the state has relied chiefly on salt certificates; Shaoxing and Chunxi reaped their benefits.

sentences.zh: 嘉定以來，二三十年之間，鈔法或行或罷，而浮鹽之說牢不可破，其害有不可勝言者。

translations.literal: Since Jiading, within twenty or thirty years, the certificate law was sometimes applied and sometimes abolished, yet the doctrine of floating/extra salt was firmly unbreakable; its harm had what could not be fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for twenty or thirty years since Jiading certificates have been toggled on and off while the floating/extra salt system has proved immovable—and the harm is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 望付有司集議，孰為可行，孰為可罷，天地之藏與官民共之，豈不甚盛？」

translations.literal: I hope it may be entrusted to the responsible offices for collective deliberation—which is feasible, which should be abolished; heaven and earth's stores shared with officials and people together—would that not be very flourishing?"
translations.idiomatic: I ask that responsible offices meet to decide what to keep and what to abolish, so heaven's bounty may be shared by state and people alike—would that not be glorious?"

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，申嚴私販苛征之禁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the prohibition against private trafficking and harsh levies was strictly proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year prohibitions on smuggling and excessive taxation were strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 寶祐元年，都省言：「行在榷貨務都茶場上本務場淳祐十二年收趁到茶鹽等錢一十一千八百一十五萬六千八百三十三貫有奇，比今新額四千萬貫增一倍以上，合視淳祐九年、十年、十一年例倍償之，以勵其後。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyou, the Imperial Secretariat said: "The temporary capital monopoly goods office's general tea field and main office field in the twelfth year of Chunyou collected tea, salt, and other cash of one billion one hundred eighty-one million five hundred sixty-eight thousand three hundred thirty-three strings odd—compared with the present new quota of forty million strings, an increase of more than double; it should follow the Chunyou ninth-, tenth-, and eleventh-year precedent for double reward, to encourage those who follow."
translations.idiomatic: In Baoyou's first year the Imperial Secretariat reported: "The temporary capital monopoly office's main tea field collected more than 1,181,568,333 strings in tea, salt, and other revenues in Chunyou twelve—more than double the new quota of forty million strings—and should receive double rewards as in Chunyou nine through eleven to encourage future performance."

sentences.zh: 有旨依所上推賞。

translations.literal: An imperial directive followed the submitted recommendation for promotion and reward.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered rewards as recommended.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，以行在務場比新額增九千一百七十三萬五千九百一十二貫有奇，本務場並三省、戶部、大府寺、交引庫，凡通管三務場職事之人，視例推賞，後以為常。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, because the temporary capital office field exceeded the new quota by ninety-one million seven hundred thirty-five thousand nine hundred twelve strings odd, the main office field together with the Three Departments, Ministry of Revenue, Grand Storehouse Directorate, and Exchange Certificate Repository—all who jointly managed the three office fields' duties—received promotion and reward by precedent; afterward this became regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year, because the temporary capital office exceeded its new quota by more than 91,735,912 strings, everyone overseeing the three monopoly offices—from the main field to the Three Departments, Ministry of Revenue, Grand Storehouse Directorate, and Exchange Certificate Repository—was rewarded by precedent, and this became standing practice.

sentences.zh: 十有二月，殿中侍御史朱熠言：「鹽近者課額頓虧，日甚一日。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Palace Attendant Censor Zhu Yi said: "Salt revenue quota has lately collapsed sharply, worsening day by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Palace Attendant Censor Zhu Yi reported: "Salt quotas have collapsed and grow worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 姑以真州分司言之，見虧二千餘萬，皆由台閫及諸軍帥興販規利之由。」

translations.literal: Take for example the Zhenzhou branch office: the visible shortfall exceeds twenty million—all from regional commanders and various army commanders engaging in trafficking to seek profit."
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhenzhou branch alone the shortfall exceeds twenty million—all because regional commissioners and army commanders trade for profit."

sentences.zh: 於是復申嚴私販之禁。

translations.literal: Thereupon the prohibition against private trafficking was again strictly proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Private trafficking was again strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 五年，朱熠復言：「 鹽之為利博矣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Zhu Yi again said: " Salt's profit is vast indeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Zhu Yi again memorialized: "The profit in salt is immense.

sentences.zh: 以蜀、廣、浙數路言之，皆不及淮鹽額之半。

translations.literal: Speaking of the several routes Shu, Guang, and Zhe, all did not reach half of Huai salt's quota.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, Guang, and Zhe together did not equal half Huai salt's quota.

sentences.zh: 蓋以斥鹵彌望，可以供煎烹，蘆葦阜繁，可以備燔燎。

translations.literal: Because brine lands stretched boundlessly to supply boiling, and reeds grew abundantly to provide fuel for firing.
translations.idiomatic: Brine flats stretched everywhere for boiling and reeds grew thick for fuel.

sentences.zh: 故環海之湄，有亭戶，有鍋戶，有正鹽，有浮鹽。

translations.literal: Therefore along the sea's shores there were saltern households, boiler households, regular quota salt, and floating/extra salt.
translations.idiomatic: Along the coast were saltern households and boiler households, regular quota salt and floating/extra salt.

sentences.zh: 正鹽出於亭戶，歸之公上者也。

translations.literal: Regular quota salt came from saltern households and was returned to the public authority.
translations.idiomatic: Regular quota salt came from saltern households and went to the state.

sentences.zh: 浮鹽出於鍋戶，鬻之商販者也，正鹽居其四，浮鹽居其一。

translations.literal: Floating/extra salt came from boiler households and was sold to peddlers; regular quota salt occupied four parts, floating/extra salt one part.
translations.idiomatic: Floating/extra salt came from boiler households and went to peddlers—four parts regular quota salt to one part floating/extra salt.

sentences.zh: 端平之初，朝廷不欲使浮鹽之利散而歸之於下，於是分置十局，以收買浮鹽，以歲額計之，二千七百九十三萬斤。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping, the court did not wish floating/extra salt profit to scatter and return to those below; thereupon ten bureaus were separately established to purchase floating/extra salt—calculated by annual quota, twenty-seven million nine hundred thirty thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duanping the court, unwilling to let floating/extra salt profits slip to private hands, set up ten bureaus to buy it up—27,930,000 jin by annual quota.

sentences.zh: 十數年來，鈔法屢更，公私俱困，真、揚、通、泰四州六十五萬袋之正鹽，視昔猶不及額，尚何暇為浮鹽計邪？

translations.literal: Over more than ten years, the certificate law was repeatedly changed; public and private both were distressed. Zhen, Yang, Tong, and Tai four prefectures' six hundred fifty thousand bags of regular quota salt, compared with former times still did not reach quota—how could there still be leisure to plan for floating/extra salt?
translations.idiomatic: For more than a decade certificate policy shifted again and again, exhausting state and people alike; the 650,000 bags of regular quota salt in Zhen, Yang, Tong, and Tai still fell short of old quotas—who had time to worry about floating/extra salt?

sentences.zh: 是以貪墨無恥之士大夫，知朝廷住買浮鹽，龍斷而籠其利；

translations.literal: Therefore greedy and shameless scholar-officials, knowing the court had halted purchase of floating/extra salt, monopolized and caged its profit;
translations.idiomatic: Greedy, shameless officials, knowing the court had stopped buying floating/extra salt, monopolized the trade for themselves;

sentences.zh: 累累灶戶，列處沙洲，日藉銖兩之鹽，以延旦夕之命；

translations.literal: Rank upon rank of oven households lined the sandbars, daily relying on ounces of salt to extend their day-to-day lives;
translations.idiomatic: saltern households lined the sandbars, living day to day on scraps of salt;

sentences.zh: 今商賈既不得私販，朝廷又不與收買，則是絕其衣食之源矣。

translations.literal: Now merchants could neither privately traffic, nor did the court purchase from them—then this cut off the source of their food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: merchants could neither sell privately nor sell to the state—their livelihood was cut off entirely.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，莫若遵端平之舊式，收鍋戶之浮鹽。

translations.literal: For the present plan, nothing is better than following the old model of the Duanping era and purchasing the floating/extra salt of boiler households.
translations.idiomatic: The best course now is to follow the Duanping precedent and buy floating/extra salt from boiler households.

sentences.zh: 所給鹽本，當過於正鹽之價，則人皆與官為市。

translations.literal: The capital paid for salt should exceed the price of regular quota salt; then everyone will trade with the government.
translations.idiomatic: If advance payments exceed the price paid for regular quota salt, everyone will sell to the state.

sentences.zh: 卻以此鹽售於上江，所得鹽息，徑輸朝廷，一則可以絕戎閫爭利之風，二則可以續鍋戶烹煎之利。」

translations.literal: Then sell this salt in the upper river region; deliver the salt profits directly to the court — first, it can end the wind of frontier commanders competing for profit; second, it can sustain the boiling profit of boiler households."
translations.idiomatic: Resell that salt in the upper Yangzi region and remit the profits straight to the court — ending frontier commanders' scramble for salt revenue while keeping boiler households in business."

sentences.zh: 有旨從之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that this be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.
